lawyer:
Mr. A.F.M. Mesbahuddin with Mr. A.K.M. Asiful Haque ------ For Petitioners
Mr. Md. Harunur Rashid ------ For the respondent No.2
parties:
M/s. Brick Linkers Ltd. and another ------ Petitioners
Versus
Joint District Judge & Others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Awlad Ali J:-"This Rule arises out of an order dated 24.4.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge and First Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka allowing the application for making preliminary decree final under Order 34 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

2. Briefly stated, the facts are that the respondent No.2 Rupali Bank Ltd. Hazaribag Branch instituted Title Suit No. 47/1994 in the 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka on 214.1994 which was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 214/1996, against the petitioner and others for realization of money amounting to Tk. 48,68,970.29 by selling the mortgaged property. The suit was decreed in preliminary form on contest on 1.6.97. The decree holder bank did not take any step immediately although the preliminary decree was sealed and signed on the same date. On 24.4.2003 the decree holder bank filed an application praying for an order making the preliminary decree dated 1.6.1997 final. The application was allowed by the learned Adalat and on the said date the final decree was sealed and signed. After the final decree was drawn up the respondent bank filed title execution case No. 114/2003 in the Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka on 28.4.2003 against the petitioner. In the execution proceedings the Adalat issued proclamation of attachment against the Vs. Joint District Judge & Ors 15 BLT ( I-1CD )2007 petitioners, and the petitioner No. 2 informed by one of the officials of the respondent bank about the filing of the title execution case. It has been contended that the trial Court which was passed the preliminary decree had no lawful authority to draw final decree after the expiry of 3 years as provided under article 181 of the Schedule to be Limitation Act and consequently the order dated 24.4.2003 making the preliminary decree final is without any lawful authority. 

3. The respondent No.2 Rupali Bank Ltd. has filed affidavit in opposition contending inter alia, that article 181 of the Schedule to this Limitation Act does not provide that after passing the preliminary decree the final decree shall have to be drawn up within 3 years from the date of preliminary decree and the Artha Rin Adalat on 24.4.2003 has drawn up the final decree in accordance with law and the final decree was put to execution decree within time. The petitioners remedy is not available under article 102 of the Constitution and as such the writ petition is not maintainable. 

4. Mr. A.F.M. Mesbahuddin the learned Advocate placing the preliminary decree dated 1.6.97 has contended that the preliminary decree annexure-D was passed by the Adalat in a suit for selling the mortgaged property of the petitioner and in terms of the decree the decree holder bank had to pray to the court for making, preliminary decree as final decree for the sale of mortgaged property in cash of the judgment debtor's in payment of the decreetal amount within 4 months. In paragraph 3 of the preliminary decree the order pissed is as follows that it is further order and decreed that in default payment as aforesaid the plaintiff may apply to the Court for a final decree for the sale of the mortgaged property or a sufficient part thereof and on such application being made a mortgaged property or a sufficient part thereof shall be directed to be sold. The operative part of the decree is in the following terms: -
“এই মোকদ্দমা দুতরফা সূত্রে ১-৪ নং বিবাদীর সহিত এবং একতরফা সূত্রে অন্যান্য বিবাদীগনের বিরুদ্ধে খরচের আদেশ সহ প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি দেওয়া হইল। বিবাদী পক্ষকে ইং ২৮-২-৯৪ তারিখ পযন্ত ৪৮,৬৮,৯৭০/২৯ (আট চল্লিশ লক্ষ আটিষট্রি হাজার নয়শত সত্তর টাকা উনত্রিশ পয়সা) টাকা এবং ইং-১/৩/৯৪ তারিখ হইতে উক্ত পরিমান টাকা আদায় পযন্ত বার্ষিক ২১/- হারে সুদসহ সমুদয় টাকা আগামী ৪(চার) মাসের মধ্যে পরিশোধ করিতে নির্দেশ দেওয়া গেল। অন্যথায় বাদী ব্যাংক বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি নিলামে বিক্রয়ের মাধ্যমে উক্ত টাকা আদায় করিয়া লইতে পারিবে।
“Mr. Mesbahuddin has argued that since specific date was given in the preliminary decree with a direction for payment of the decreetal amount within 4(four) months, the right to apply to make the preliminary decree final accrued after the expiry of 4(four) months. The decree holder Bank having not applied for making the decree final within three years from the date when four months expired the application made by the decree holder bank ought not to have been entertained by the Adalat. The application was barred under Article 181 of the Limitation Act. Since the decree was sealed and signed on 1.6.97 and the decree holder bank made application on 24.4.2003 which is after more than 5 years the Adalat has no lawful authority to make the decree final as per the provision as laid down under Order 34 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure as 3 years time as proved under Article 181 of the Limitation Act. He contends that time expired long before even the decree holder bank had not any legal right to apply to the Court for making the preliminary decree final after the expiry of the period prescribed by the law of limitation. The further contention raised by the learned Advocate is that since the order dated 24.4.2003 making the preliminary decree final was made beyond statutory period such decree is not executable and the title execution case No. 114 of 2003 is liable to be stuck down. 

5. Article 181 as provided in the First Schedule Third Division of the Limitation Act is as under: 
Description-of application 	    Period of limitation         Time from which period begins to run. 
181-Application for which no            (three years)              When the right to apply accrues
period of limitation is provided 
or by section 48 of the Code of 
Civil Procedure , 1908 (V of 1908) 

6. Mr. Mesbahuddin has at least cited 2 decision of Indian jurisdiction on the proposition that the application should be filed within 3 years from the date when the right to apply accrued. One is the case of Mahamad Kamal Vs. Ahmed Ali and others reported in 87IC (1925)-746 and other case is Gajanan Chintaman Deshpande and others Vs. Karnatak Glass Industries and others reported in AIR 1971-Mysore, 241. The principle enunciated there is that the decree holders right to apply to make the preliminary decree final under order XXXIV rule 5 C, P. Code accrued after the expiry of the time given in the preliminary decree for payment of money and unless the application is made within 3 years from the dare when the right accrued the application would be barred under Article 181 of the Limitation Act. 

7. Mr. Harunur Rashid the learned Advocate representing the Bank on the other hand contended that Article 181 of the Limitation Act has no manner of application and the Court which passed the preliminary decree had ample power to make the decree final even after the period of 3 years because the drawing up of final decree is a mere legal formality and the decree holder had the right to apply to the court to make the preliminary decree final at any time for the purpose of selling the mortgage property for satisfying the terms of the preliminary decree. There is no rule that the decree should be drawn up within 3 years. In support of his submission he cited a decision in the case of Chhaganlal Sakarlal Vani Vs. Jayaram Deoraj Thakar and others reported in 100 IC 956 which was decided in civil appellate jurisdiction where it has been stated that: 
"As regards the first point, it is perfectly true to say that there was a preliminary decree passed, and there was the order making the decree for sale absolute, but there was no formal final decree drawn up. Technically, therefore, it is right to say that there is no final decree which could be executed. This contention' has become possible because of the laxity which prevails in the lower Courts in drawing up decree in mortgage suit. In the present case the preliminary decree was r. Vs. Joint District Judge & Ors 15BLT (I-ICD) 2007 drawn up in the proper form provided by the Code of Civil Procedure. Under Rule 5 of Order 34, when such payment as is directed by the preliminary decree is not made, the Court shall, on an application made in that behalf by the plaintiff, pass as decree that the mortgaged property or a sufficient part thereof be sold. And when an order making the decree absolute is made, the final decree has to be drawn up. The question that now arises is whether at this distance of time, nearly 15 years after the decree, and 12 years after the order making the decree absolute was made, the execution can go on or not. 
Having regard to the terms of the preliminary decree which has been made absolute we could only attribute the omission to have a final decree drawn up to a misapprehension on the part of the Court, as well as the parties concerned as to the necessity of having final decree formally drawn up." 

8. It seems to us from the above that in the above case in the preliminary decree there was an order making the decree for sale absolute. Therefore, the preposition is not relevant at all to decide the issue before us. Two other decisions namely A.I.R.1918 Patna 4 land 30 D.L.R.424 seem to be not applicable in the facts of the present case. 

9.Overwhelming decisions of the- sub continental jurisdiction, particularly in the appellate, jurisdiction in a civil matter dealing with Order 34 Rule 5 and under section 181 of the Limitation Act, suggestion that in a Mortgage Suit where the order is made in the preliminary decree directing the judgment debtor to pay the decretal dues within certain specified dates and if payment is not made according to the direction and the time given, in that case the decree holder must make the applicable for making the preliminary decree final within 3 years after the expiry of that specified time, in other words the right to apply will accrue to the decree holder after the time given in the preliminary decree just passed. In the case of Cawnpore Municipal Board Vs. Pt. Tirjugi Narain reported in A.I.R.1947 Allahabad 82 (D.B) it has been observed that it is obvious that the application dated 24.4.2003 for the preparation of the final decree in accordance with the decree of this Court was beyond 3 years and was clearly barred by Article 181 Limitation Act 1908 similar view was expressed in the case of Bhajanmal Topandas and others Vs. Tikam das Thakurdas and others reported in A.I.R.1947 Sind 12. 

10. We are not concerned with the proposition as to whether the provision of Order 34 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure was wrongly or rightly applied by the Adalat in exercise of its power under the Code of Civil Procedure. The Adalat having' assumed jurisdiction under the Code of Civil Procedure may rightly or wrongly decide the question under the particular provision of law, but when the statute namely Limitation Act provides for and prescribes a time limit to do any act or pass any order under the Civil Procedure Code and the Court or Adalat does that act or pass any order going beyond that prescribed time limit that becomes without jurisdiction and Court having failed to exercise its power under Order 34 Rule 5 in making the preliminary decree dated 1.6.97 final within 3 years from the date when the right to make an application by the decree holder accrued, the impugned order dated 24.4.2003 appears to be without jurisdiction, because that order not only was passed beyond the statutory period but that also affected the rights of the parties, the judgment debtors. It is further noticeable from the impugned order that no notice was served upon the judgment debtor petitioner before making the preliminary decree final to hear the judgment debtor. In a writ of certiorari writ cannot issue to correct the mistake or wrong done in exercise of the power under the C.P. Code but in instance case the Artha Rin Adalat passed the impugned order and exercised its power going beyond the statutory period of limitation which cannot be otherwise excluded and as such the order is without jurisdiction and is liable to be struck down. 

11. Before parting with the judgment it may be mentioned that at the time of delivery of the judgment it appears that the learned Advocate Mr. Harunur Rashid did not file any power on behalf of the bank. On query he is unable to make any positive reply. 

12. In view of the Rule is made absolute. The order dated 24.4.2003 is set aside and consequence will follow that there is no executable decree before the Adalat. 

13. Having regard to the facts of the case there will be no order as to costs.

	End.

lawyer:
Mr. Nuro Nabi --- For the petitioners.
Mr. Md. Mozammel Hoque Bhuiyan with Mr. S.M. Selim --- For the opposite party.
parties:
Md. Zia Bepari and others ----- Petitioners.
Versus
Sheikh Abu Taher ----- Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
Ms. Salma Masud Chowdhury, j:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 25.9.2005 (decree signed on 2.10.2005) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, lst Court, Munshiganj in Title Appeal No.I42 of 2004 dismissing the same and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 8.9.2004 (decree signed on 11.9.2004) passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Shirajdikhan, Munshiganj in Title Suit No. 124 of 2002 decreeing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The opposite party No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 124 of 2002 in the Court of Senior Assistant, Judge, 1st Court, Shirajdikhan, Munshiganj impleading the petitioners as defendants, seeking for a decree of permanent injunction. 

3. The defendant petitioners contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. 

4. The trial Court decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 8.9.2004 and 11.9.2004 respectively. 

5. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendants preferred appeal before the District Judge, Munshiganj which was transferred to the court of the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Munshiganj for disposal, who dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25,9.2005 and 2.10.2005 respectively. 

6. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendants as petitioners filed an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

7. Mr. Nuro Nabi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the Courts below misread and misconstrued the evidence on record and thereby committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit. He next submits that both the Courts below failed to appreciate that the unregistered sale deed alleged to have been executed in favour of the vendors of the plaintiffs was a forged and an antedated one and the Courts below decreed the suit by putting reliance on the said forged deeds. He also points out that the plaintiff could not prove his possession on the suit land but on the other hand, the defendants by adducing evidence proved their possession on the suit land and the Courts below failed to appreciate that the defendants are claiming the suit land by way of inheritance and the S.A. and R.S. records in the name of the plaintiff are not the exclusive proof of possession and thus it cannot be the basis for deciding the matter in question. He also submits that for ends of justice, the matter may be referred to the trial Court for rehearing on remand. He submits that the suit land was not properly demarcated by metes and bounds and no order of injunction can be passed on an unspecified land. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 50 D.L.R.(AD) page 188. He also points out that during the pendency of the present revision another title suit being Title suit No.35 of 2006 was filed before the Senior Assistant Judge. Munshiganj under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act for recovery of khas possession regarding the selfsame suit land, Which is fixed for preemptory hearing. The learned Advocate for the petitioners referred some decisions in support to his contentions made before this Court as reported in 50 D.L.R.(AD) page 188, 50 D.L.R.(H.C,) page 271, 39 D.L.R.(H.C.) page 8. He submits that section 9 of the Specific Relief Act does not authorise the Court to order for demolishing or removing dwelling huts or other permanent structures in the suit land while effecting restoration of possession. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 50 D.L.R.(H.C.) page-271. He next submits that when a person is dispossessed from any immovable property, he may file a suit to recover possession thereof, and the question of title will not be a matter of decision in that suit and under the provision of section 9 of the Specific Relief Act removal of structures raised by the defendant on the property cannot be ordered. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 39 D.L.R.(H.C.) page 8. The learned Advocate submits that during the pendency of the present Civil Revision the petitioner got possession on the suit land and made structures on it which cannot be removed now. 

8. Mr. Md. Mozammel Hoque Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 files a counter affidavit and submits that the plaintiff has succeeded to prove his case before the Courts below and accordingly relief was granted to him. He next submits that considering the facts, circumstances and evidence on record, the trial Court decreed the suit and the lower appellate Court affirmed the judgment passed by the trial Court on the basis of materials on record and there being no error in the decision being occasioned to the defendant petitioners, the Rule is liable to be discharged. The learned Advocate submits that the plaintiff being the sole owner of the suit land obtained the D.C.R. by mutation operation and was paying rent regularly and the Courts below found prima-facie right, title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and granted injunction as prayed for. Pie submits that the petitioner dispossessed the plaintiff opposite party from the suit land showing delinquent attitude to the judgments and decrees of the Courts below. 

9. I have heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners and the opposite party No. 1 and perused the revisional application, counter affidavit along with other materials on record. It appears that the trial Court decreed the suit of the plaintiff opposite party for permanent injunction and the judgment and decree as passed by the trial Court was affirmed by the Court of appeal below but before filing the revisional application before this Court, the plaintiff was dispossessed from the property in question by the defendant petitioners. A party altering the status-quo existing at the time of filing of the suit or proceeding must be compelled to restore the status-quo. 'In the present case the plaintiff opposite party was in possession of the suit property and the Courts below finding prima-facie title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land granted a decree of permanent injunction and, the defendant opposite party, when the said decree was in existence in favour of the plaintiff, altered the physical possession of the plaintiff and dispossessed him from the suit land defying Court's order. A person who is aware of an order of the Court is bound to obey the same. Order 21 Rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that where the party against whom a decree for the Specific Performance of a contract, or for restitution of conjugal rights, or for an injunction, has been passed, has had an. opportunity of obeying the decree and has willfully failed to obey it, the decree may be enforced in the case of a decree for restitution of conjugal rights by the attachment of his property or, in the case of a decree for the Specific Performance of a Contract or for an injunction, by his detention in the civil prison, or by the attachment of his property, or by both. This Rule makes specific provisions for execution of decree for injunction. In the present case, the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court considered all aspects thoroughly and concurrently found that the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree of permanent injunction. 

10. The decisions of both the Courts below, being based on facts, circumstances and evidence on record and there being concurrent findings over the points in issues and there being found no error of law or fact in passing the impugned judgment, 1 am of the opinion that the impugned judgments and decrees do not warrant any interference by this Court. 

11. Since both the Courts below on proper assessment of the evidence on record came to a concurrent finding, this finding is binding upon this Court, unless it is shown that there is misreading or non-consideration of material evidence on record in arriving to such finding. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has failed to make out such a case. 

12. The judgments of the. Courts below are not tainted with any legal infirmity and perversity justifying interference. After examining the record of the case and hearing the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of both the parties, 1 am of the view that there are sufficient evidence and materials on record to come to the decisions which have been arrived at by the Courts below. In the present case, I find that during the existence of a decree passed by the trial Court which has been affirmed by the Court of appeal below, the present petitioners who are the defendant; dispossessed the plaintiff opposite party from the suit land although the plaintiff has a decree in his favour for permanent injunction and after dispossessing the plaintiffs, the defendant as petitioners filed the present Civil Revision. The petitioners have flouted the Court's order and showed disrespect and dishonor to the judgments and decrees passed by Courts which is a total disregard for the machinery of justice and with a criminal attitude, after dispossessing the plaintiffs and getting into the possession of the suit land, filed a suit for simple declaration of title. The defendant petitioners have committed a criminal offence by disobeying a decree of permanent injunction and the decree shall be enforced by resort of Order 21 Rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

13. In the result, true is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgments of the Courts below stand maintained. The trial Court is directed to take steps against the defendant petitioners under Order 21 Rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and restore possession to the plaintiff opposite party keeping in view the decree as passed in Title Suit No. 124 of 2002. 


14. Send down the lower Court records and a copy of the judgment and order to the court concerned. 

End.

caseno: Writ Petition No.6929 of 2004 and 6930 of 2004
lawyer:
Mr. S. N. Goswami, Advocate For the Petitioner in both the Rules 
Mr. Shaheb Ali Zinnah. Advocate ------ For the Respondent No.2 In Writ petition No.6930 of 2004
parties:
Md. Arfan Uddin Akand ------ Petitioner in Writ Petition No.6929 of 2004
With
Md. Kamal Uddin Akand ------ Petitioner. In Writ Petition No.6930 012004
Versus
Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No Gazipur and Another ------ Respondents In both the Writ Petitions
full_judgment:
Mr. Mirza Hussain Haider. J: In both these Rules, the point so raised and the facts being similar are taken up together to be disposed of accordingly by this single judgment. 

2. The question raised in both the Rules is whether the judgment and. decree dated 15.9.2004 (in writ petition No.6929/2004) and dated 10.9.2004 (in writ  petition No.6930 of 2004) passed by the Artha Rin Gazipur, in their respective Artha Rin suits under Section 13 should not -be declared to have been passed without lawful authority. 

3. The common facts in both the Rules, in short, are that the respondent No.2. Bangladesh Krishi Bank Shreepur Branch Gazipur instituted suit against the petitioners of both the Rule for realisation of loan obtained by them for the purpose of running their respective business of Poultry Firm. The petitioners being unable to pay off the loan within the stipulated period the hank issued several notices upon them but without any result. Subsequently, the bank filed Artha Rin Suit No.78of 2004 against the petitioner ii writ petition No.6929 of 2004 and Artha, RM. Suit No. 70 of 2004 against petitioner of Writ petition No. 6930 of 2004. The petitioner or both the writ petitions entered appearance in the suits and filed their respective written statements denying the material allegations contained in the plaints. Thereupon the defendants in both the snits i.e. the petitioners In these two Rules, tiled application under Order XXVI Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure -for appointment of Commissioner to examine the accounts of their respective Cash Credit accounts. Conversely, the respondent hank also filed applications under section 13th of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 2003 (hereinafter referred to as the said Ain) for delivery of judgment on the ground that the, defendants have admitted the claims of-the plaintiff bank. 'The Adalat thereafter, fixed a date for hearing of both the applications filed under order XXVI Rule 1.1 of the Code, and section 13(1) of the Ain, 2003 - whereupon the Adalat rejected the prayers of the defendants under order 26 Rule 11 of the Code and allowed the applications of the plaintiff bank under section 13 (1) of The Ain and accordingly, delivered 'the impugned judgments and decreed the suit under section 13(1) of the Ain 2003. 

4. Against which these two Rules have been obtained by the petitioners. 

5. Mr. Goswami the learned Advocate appearing behalf of the petitioners in both the writ petition that the provision of section 13 of the Ain has not been complied with by the Adalat while decreeing the suit. He submits that the said provision of law provided for perusal and consideration of the pleadings of both the parties and then come to -a conclusion as to whether  respective issues are required to be framed or there being- no material to frame issues decree the suit accordingly. As such submits that the Adalat did not, at all consider that the defendants did not admit the entire claim of the plaintiff-bank. Rather on the facts and circumstances of the cases as derived from the two written statements and their applications under  order XXV Rule 11 Of the code for examining  their respective accounts by a Commissioner appointed by the Adalat it would be apparent that there are anomalies and irregularities in the claim of the plaintiff -bank. Referring to' the provision of section 13 of the Ain Mr. Goswami submits that the Maim.. neither considered them written statements as whole nor came to a conclusion upon considering the facts and circumstances as stated in the pleadings of the parties, as provided for in section '13(4) while passing the impugned orders and as such the judgment and decree complained herein, passed by the -Adalat under section 13(1) of the Ain are illegal and without jurisdiction and the same are liable to be set aside. Referring to the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent bank Mr. Goswami next submits that no doubt the judgments and decree have been challenged in both the .Rules but there is no bar in challenging the same under the writ jurisdiction if the same appears to have been passed without jurisdiction and if the same is found to be perverse and illegal. In this Artha Rin Adalat & Ors (Mira: Hussain Haider, P345 respect he relied on the ease of The Mayor. Chittagong City corporation Chittagong and others V. Mohammad Jahangir Faruk and others reported in 131. (AD) 24 and submits that the view taken by the High Court Division as no appeal was filed against order of dismissal the writ petition so filed challenging legality of the order is very much maintainable" has been upheld by the Appellate Division in the aforesaid decision. So he submits that since the impugned judgment and decree is palpably illegal, perverse and without jurisdiction seeking relief /redress under Article 102 of the constitution is -very much maintainable. In, the question of maintainability of the writ petition instead of not availing the forum of appeal provided in the statute, he draw our attention to the decision in the case of ETV Ltd. and another Vs. Bangladesh and others, reported in 10. BLT (AD) 108.Referring to the paragraph No.46 of the said decision, Mr. Goswami submits that the  fundamental rights like rule of law are to be measured in our human beings i.e. the judges by applying law. Therefore, there will always be an element of discretion to be used by the Court in giving standing to the petitioner. He submits that the Appellate Division in the said judgment, relying on the aforesaid view observed" from the above, it appears that the courts of this jurisdiction has shifted its position to a great extent from the traditional rule of standing which confines access to the judicial process only to those to whom legal injuries caused or legal wrong is done. The narrow confines within which the rule or standing was imprisoned for long years have been broken and new dimension is being given to the doctrine of locus standi". Referring to the view of the Appellate Division he submits that time has came for this Division to extend its hand to safeguard the interest of the poor litigant to whom legal injuries are caused and for legal wrong is being done. As such the provision of Article 102 is very much exercisable in this respect where in the lower judiciary has passed the Judgment and decree which is palpably illegal Perverse and without jurisdiction. For that purpose he submits that the door of justice should not be shut down on the ground of available alternative remedy. Lastly he submits that all the requirements of section 8 (2) of the Ain. so far it relates to the specific statements to be made in a particular schedule as to the principal amount of loan, amount of simple and penal interest etc has not been complied with in the plaint itself, which have been reflected in the application filed under order 26 Rule 11 of the code and as such the Adalat committed illegality in rejecting the said application without. Considering the entire circumstances stated there in and thereby did not give-any .opportunity to the petitioners to move the higher court against such rejection orders and without framing any issue of the said particular dispute decreed the suit under section 13(1) of the Ain.2003.As such the impugned judgments and decree are palpably illegal and without jurisdiction. 

6. On the other hand Mr. Zinnah. the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent bank in writ petition 6930 of 2004 submits that the Appellate Division reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191 in the case of Zahirul Islam Vs. National Bank and in the case of G.M Toufiq Vs. Agrani Bank and another reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6 held that filing of writ petition against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat without availing specific forum of appeal as laid down in the Ain itself, are not maintainable. He submits that whenever the judgment and decree is passed the aggrieved party has the remedy, of challenging the same before the appellate forum as provided for in the Ain itself upon depositing the amount prescribed in the said Ain within the stipulated time and for that purpose writ petition is not maintainable. As such filing of the writ petition under such circumstances has been discouraged the Appellate Division. Therefore, the Rules being obtained challenging the legality -of the judgment and decree the same are not maintainable in the eve of law and as such the submissions made by Mr. Goswami on the question so math on merit of the Rule art sustainable in law. 

7. Though the respondents filed affidavit in opposition in writ petition No.6929 of 2004 but no one appeared to substantiate the 'same. 

8. We have perused the writ petitions along with the annex tires annexed thereto. it is true that the appellate Division in the aforesaid decisions has held that special provision for appeal having been made for challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin  Adalat no application under Article 102 o the constitution lies against the same. Again, in the case of Zahirul Islam reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191 the Appellate Division held that the question of limitation and in excess of the Court's jurisdiction are matters to be agitated in appeal not under the writ, petition and the aforesaid view of the aforesaid decision has been affirmed by the Appellate Division in the case of Bangladesh Agriculture Development Corporation Vs. Artha Rin Adalat and others reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6.But again in the case of Managing Director. Rupali Bank Ltd and others Vs. Tafazal Hossain and others reported in DLR (AD) 260 the Appellate Division held that the jurisdiction of the court goes to the cry root of the matter brought before it and of the court got no jurisdiction everything shall fall through under such circumstances let us now see whether the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Adalat under section 13(1) of the Ain 2003 are in excess of jurisdiction. For the purpose let us see section 13 as has been provided in the statue. Section 13 reads as follow:
“১৩। মামলার বিচার্য্য বিষয় গঠন ও নিষ্পত্তি।-১। বিবাদী কর্তৃক লিখিত জবাব দাখিল হওয়ার পরবর্তীতে ধার্য্য একটি নির্ধারিত তারিখে আদালত উভয় পক্ষকে, যদি উপস্থিত থাকে, শুনানী করিয়া এবং আরজি ও লিখিত বর্ণনা পর্যালোচনা করিয়া মামলার বিচার্য্য বিষয়, যদি থাকে, গঠন করিবে, এবং যদি বিচার্য্য বিষয় না থাকে, আদালত অবিলম্বে রায় বা আদেশ প্রদান করিবে।
(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এ নির্ধারিত তারিখে, কোন বা উভয় পক্ষ যদি অনুপস্থিত থাকে, তাহা হইলে আদালত, আরজি ও লিখিত বর্ণনা পর্যালোচনা করিয়া মামলার বিচার্য্য বিষয়, যদি থাকে, গঠন করিবে, এবং যদি বিচার্য্য বিষয় না থাকে, আদালত অবিলম্বে রায় বা আদেশ প্রদান করিবে।
(৩) মামলার যে কোন পর্যায়ে, লিখিত বর্ণনায় কিংবা অন্য কোন ভাবে বিবাদী কর্তৃক বাদীর আর্জির বক্তব্য স্বীকৃত হইয়া থাকিলে, এবং উক্তরূপ স্বীকৃতির ভিত্তিতে যেরুপ রায় বা আদেশ প্রার্থনা করিয়া বাদী আদালতের নিকটে দরখাস্ত করিলে, আদালত, বাদী ও বিবাদীর মধ্যে বিদ্যমান অপরাপর বিচার্য্য বিষয় নিষ্পত্তির জন্য অপেক্ষা না করিয়া, উপযুক্ত রায় বা আদেশ প্রদান করিবে।
৪। মামলার শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য্য প্রথম তারিখে অথবা মামলার যে কোন পর্যায়ে যদি আদালতের নিকট প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, পক্ষদ্বয়ের মধ্যে ঘটনা অথবা আইনগত বিষয়ে কোন বিবাদ নেই, তাহা হইলে আদালত, অবিলম্বে রায় বা আদেশ প্রদান করিয়া মামলা চুড়ান্ত নিষ্পত্তি করিবে।”

9. Upon reading section 13 it is clear that after filling of the written statement the court on a subsequent date upon hearing both the parties if they are present and on perusal of the plaint and written statement will frame issue. If there be any and if there is no issue to be framed then the court may dispose of the suit No delivering judgment or order. That means i he court will have to peruse the plaint and written 4atCfllcni filed by both me parties k 113 a subsequent date and come to a conclusion as to whether issues are to be brander judgment and order is to be delivered. Again, in section 13(3) it has been categorically stated that on perusal of the written statement if it appears to the emit that the defendant admitted the claim of the plaintiff the court can pass judgment or on the basis Of such admission. This may he done even before deciding any other issues if framed. Again section 13(4) on the other hand, categorically says that when the Wart will he of the opinion at any stage of the suit that there is no dispute between the parties as regards the fact and circumstances or the law then the court can dispose of the suit finally. Sp, on perusal of the aforesaid provisions of law it appears that the court before passing any judgment or order or finally disposing of the suit shall have to take into consideration the facts stated in the plaint and written statement of the parties and to determine that whether the defendants admit the claim of the plaintiff and also to determine whether there is any dispute between the parties as regards the facts as stated in the pleadings. Now if we see the impugned judgments and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in the respective Rules then -it will appear that the Adalat while rejection the application under order XXVI Rule II of the code challenged in writ petition No.6929 of 2004 observed:
“শুনানী অন্তে এবং কাগজপত্র পর্যালোচনাক্রমে বিবাদী পক্ষের দরখাস্তটি নাকচ করা হইল।”
On these findings the Adalat passed the impugned judgment and decreed the suit. Accordingly, the same has been challenged in writ petition No.6029 of 2004. In the impugned judgment and decree it appear, that the Adalat did not make any finding of its own that whether the defendant admitted the claim of the plaintiff rather relied on the application of the plaintiff wherein it has been stated:
“বিবাদীপক্ষ জবাবে ঋণ গ্রহনের কথা স্বীকার করিয়াছে। এ পর্যায়ে অপরাপর বিষয় সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন না করিয়াই আদালত বাদী পক্ষের দরখাস্তের ভিত্তিতে মোকদ্দমায় যথাযথ রায় ঘোষনার সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন করেন।”

10. On the-other hand. the application under order XXVI Rule Ii shows that the fads and circumstances of the plaint has been disputed by the defendant and on perusal of the written statement it appears that there is no mention of admission of the plaintiffs claim. Mr. Goswami took us through the written statement and he pointed out that There is no specific assertion of the defendant as to admission of the plaintiffs claim in their written statement. -So- if there is no specific admission made in the written .statement as contemplated in section 9 (5) of the Ain.. the Adalat cannot -come to conclusion as  regards the said  fact of the case. But, the Adalat while decreeing_ the suits under section 13 (1) simply observed: 
“এ পর্যায়ে অপরাপর বিষয় সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন না করিয়ািই আদালতে বাদী পক্ষের দরখাস্তের ভিত্তিতে মোকদ্দমায় যথাযথ রায় ঘোষনার সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন করেন।”
Thus it appears that the Adalat did not consider the pleadings of the defendant nor considered that there are disputes as regards the facts of the case and as s.uch the passing of the impugned judgment under section 13(1) appears to be wholly without jurisdiction.

11. In writ petition No. 6930 of 2004 on perusal of the impugned order it appears that the Adalat while passing the impugned judgment and decree upon rejecting the application under order XXVI Rule 11 held that there is no sufficient reasons o appoint a commissioner and there Ring no material for framing issues the suit is taken up for disposal under section 13 (1) and there after the Adalat categorically held: 
“অপরদিকে বিবাদীপক্ষ মোকদ্দমার সমন প্রাপ্ত হইয়া লিখিত জবাব দাখিল করিয়াছেন জবাবে বিবাদীপক্ষ বাদীর আরজী বর্নিত মোতাবেক ঋনের টাকা গ্রহনের কথা এড়ানোর চেষ্টা করিলেও জবাবের ৮ম দফায় উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন যে, বিবাদী ঋনের টাকা পরিশোধ করিতে ইচ্ছুক। যাহা ঋন গ্রহনের কথা স্বীকৃত স্বরুপঃ”

 12. On perusal of the same it appears that unlike in the other Rule the Adalat applied its mind in considering the written statement and specifically came to a conclusion that the defendant has admitted in the paragraph No.8 of the written statement as to the loan. Such finding is the result of the application of the learned Judge's mind. Thus on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree it is clear that the Adalat perused the pleadings of the parties found that there is admission of the defendant as to the claim and also perused the facts alleged by the parties and came to such findings that defendant has admitted the claim of the plaintiff and as such took up the cake for disposal under section 13. So in this Rule it is found that the Adalat though rejected the application under order XXV1 Rule 11 of the Code Without assigning any reason but the finding arrived at as to disposal of the suit is in accordance with law and upon compliance of the provision of section 9 add 13. So, in our view the impugned order challenged in Writ petition No.6930 of 2004 passed by the Adalat is not without jurisdiction. 

13. Considering the facts and circumstances stated here in above, it can be said that when the Adalat passed the impugned judgment beyond the scope of law as provided .for in section 13 of the Ain then it can he said that the same is without jurisdiction. But when it appears from the impugned judgment that the same is passed upon complying with the provision of section 13 it cannot be said that the same is without jurisdiction. 
'Considering the decisions referred above and discussions made herein above, we are of the view that lithe Adalat basses any order which is wholly without jurisdiction not in excess of jurisdiction then despite of the fact that the law provided forum for appeal, the petitioner cannot be debarred from availing the jurisdiction under Article 102 of the constitution. Because the question of jurisdiction or the Court goes to the very root of the matter brought before it and when the court does not have any jurisdiction to see, everything done subsequent thereto 'Shall fall through and the Court which has got no jurisdiction to pass such order over the matter shall not 5.to into the merit of the matter as decided in the case of the case of Managing Director, Rupali Bank Ltd. And others Vs. Tafazal Hossain and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 260. 

14. Accordingly we Uind that the Rule in Writ Petition N0.6"-) 29 4)1 7:004 has merit and the Rule in Writ Petitioning No.6930 of 2004 these not have any 0:erit. 

15. In the result the Rule in \Air Petition no.6929 of 2004 is made absolute. 'File suit is sent back to the trial court with direction. that the Artiut kin Adalat frame issues on perusal of the plaint the written statement filed by the parties for deciding the case on merit and dispose of the same in accordance with law. 

16. The Rule in Writ Petition NO.6930 co; 2004 is discharged. There will been order as to costs. 

	End.
