full_judgment:
Mr. Siddiqur Rahman Miah, J.: This revisional, application at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the judgment and order dated 13.04.1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First court, Gazipur, in Review Miscellaneous case No. 17 of 1995 rejecting an application for review of judgment and decree dated 13.02.1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.966 of 1985 dismissing the suit. 

2. The plaintiff petitioner instituted Title suit being ultimately numbered as Title Suit No.966 of 1985 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Gazipur praying for declaration that the plaintiff is the 16 annas owner of the suit land as described in the schedule to the plaint; that the document No. 5839 dated 15.10.1928 and document No.1385 dated 02.11.1931 is forged, fraudulent, void and not binding upon the plaintiff and that the RS and SA record were not correct and further prayed for recovery of khas possession of the suit land. 

3. The case of the plaintiff petitioner in short is that the suit jama originally belonged to one Meher Ali who died leaving behind one son Darbesh Ali and 2(two) daughters namely Goljan and Peary Begum and that the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Darbesh Ali in the CS record excluding his two sisters; that the property left behind by Meher Ali. legally devolved on his son and 2 daughters; that Darbesh Ali got 8 annas and each sister got 4 annas; that thereafter Darbesh Ali died leaving behind his sisters as his only heirs who inherited the suit jama in 8 annas share of her brother. It is further stated that subsequently Goljan Bibi died leaving behind her only sister Peary Begum as her heir; that thus Peary Begum became the 16 annas owner of the property of Meher Ali; that Peary Begum, owning and possessing the suit property, transferred the same to one Kofiluddin, the father of the present plaintiff petitioner, by Heba-bill-Ewaz dated 29.01.1927 and handed over the possession of the suit property to Kofiluddin and that after the death of Kofiluddin, his only son Shafiuddin got the suit land as legal heir of Kofiluddin; that the defendant opposite parties had no right, title, interest and possession over the suit property. 

4. It is also stated that as the plaintiff petitioner was minor at the time of death of his father the defendants always tried to take possession of the suit property forcibly taking advantage of his minority and ultimately on 20.06.1978 the defendants evicted the petitioner's predecessor from the suit land and took possession of the same.

5. It is further Stated that Peary Begum sold her .95 acres of land by registered kabala dated 15.10.1928; that the property of Kofiluddin allegedly purchased by Nazimuddin and Mokbar Ali by registered deed No. 1388 dated 02.11.1931; and that those documents have been manufactured with intent to grab the property of the plaintiff petitioner. Hence the suit for declaration for declaring those documents forged, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff petitioner. 

6. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing joint written statement on 12.07.1982 and again, defendants Nos. I and 2 filed additional written statement. In the meantime the defendant No.1 Ahad Ali died and his heirs was substituted as the defendant No. 1 (Ka), 1 (cha) and defendant No. 2 filed joint Additional written statement on 14.09.1992 along with defendant No.3 and thus they contested the suit. 

7. The case of the defendant, in short, is that, they, acquiring the suit land have been owning and possessing the suit land paying rent to the government. The further case of the defendant is that the plaintiff has got no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land; that the defendants have been owning and possessing the suit land for more then 60 years by creating house on it and the assertion of the plaintiff that he has been dispossessed from the suit land is not correct and that the plaintiff is, not entitled to get any relief in this suit and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

8. The plaintiff examined 4 witnesses including the plaintiff petitioner Shafiuddin alias Shafi as PW1 while the defendants examined 3 DWs including Baset Sarker, a son of opposite party No. 3-Kamaljan. The plaintiff submitted some papers and documents in support of his contention which are marked as exhibit 1 to 4, while the defendants submitted some documents in support of his contention which are marked exhibits as 'Ka' to 'Tha'. 

9. The learned Subordinate Judge. First court, Gazipur framed as many as 7(seven) issues. He considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 13.02.1995. 

10. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 13.02.1995, the plaintiff filed review Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1995 under order 47 Rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure but the learned trial court rejected the application for review by his judgment and order dated 13.04.1996. It is against the judgment and order dated 13.04.1996 the plaintiff preferred this revisional application before this court and obtained the present Rule. 

11. Mr. Faruque Ahmed with Mr. K. S. Hossain the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned trial court erred in not considering a most silent aspect of the case that the learned trial court did not pass any order in connection with the amendment of the plaint relating to decree passed in title Suit No. 133 of 1916. He further submits that the review application is not barred by limitation as the petitioner filed this application for review within the period of 90 days and in this connection he refers the decision in the case of Shawkat Ara Begum vs. Md. Wajuddin and others reported in 2 BLT (HCD) 226 and submits that the period of limitation for filing the review application as per Article 173 of Limitation Act is 90 days. But the learned Subordinate Judge wrongly held that the period of limitation is 30 days and calculating 30 days for limitation he illegally help that the review petition is barred by limitation. It is further submitted that as the petitioner filed the review petition well within 90 days and as such the petition is not barred by limitation. 

12. The learned Advocate for the petitioner referred the decision in the case of Azifa Khatun vs. Tulshi Ranjan Roy, reported in 37 DLR 268 in support of this contention where in their Lordship held that no wrong can go without a remedy and a suitor cannot be punished for the wrong done to him by the court itself. 

13. Mr. F.R.M. Nazrul Ahsan, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that review application under order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed beyond the statutory period of 90 days without explaining the causes of delay; that grounds stated in the revisional application are those of memorandum of appeal and not of review of the judgment and decree and if those grounds are considered, the original suit would have to he reopened for disposal on merits which is foreign to the provision of the order 47, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

14. He further submits that the petitioner failed to show- discovery of any new and important matter or evidence, which after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge, or could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed. He further submits that the petitioner in his review petition failed to show any mistake or error apparent on the face of the record and thus the learned trial court committed no wrong while passing the judgment and order in review petition and as such the revisional application is liable to be set aside. 

15. The learned advocate for the opposite parties refers the decision in the case of Abul Hossain and 3 others vs. Bangladesh represented by Secretary, Ministry of land and others reported in 51 DLR (AD) 16 and the decision in the case of Arun Bhowmik and others vs. Selim Reza and others reported in 40 DLR 199 in support of his contention. 

16. The only point of consideration is whether the learned Subordinate Judge, committed any error of law resulting in an error in passing the impugned judgment and order-dated 13.04.1996. 

17. The case of the plaintiffs petitioners it appears from record that the petitioners filed an application for amendment of plaint on 28.02.1987 under order 6, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure to the effect that a suit being No. 133 of 1916 was instituted for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of suit land which was finally decreed on compromise in terms of solenama filed by the plaintiffs and the defendant No. 1 Guljan Bibi. It is also the contention of the petitioners that the learned trial court fixed the date of hearing on 22.06.87 and the same application was again fixed on 24.06.87 for hearing and order. But the learned Subordinate Judge without disposing of that application for amendment illegally dismissed the case. It is the further contention of the petitioners that if the application for amendment was taken into the consideration the result of the suit would have been in their favour. 

18. It is the contention of the petitioners that the learned Subordinate Judge without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and law relating thereto rejected the prayer for review by his judgment and order dated 13.04.1996. 

19. Now let us see whether the learned Subordinate Judge committed any error of law. Matter of review relates to under order 47, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil procedure which runs thus: 

(1) Any person considering himself aggrieved-

(a) by a decree or order from which an appeal is allowed, but from which no appeal has been preferred.

(b) by a decree or order from which no appeal is allowed 

(c) by a decision on a reference from a court of small causes, 

and who, from the discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed or order made, or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or for any other sufficient reason, desires to obtain a review of the decree passed or order made against him may apply for a review of judgment to the court which passed the decree or made the order." 

20. The provision relating to review constitutes an exception to the general rule that once the judgment is signed and pronounced by the court it has no jurisdiction to alter it. 

21. Section 114 of the Code gives a substantive right of review in certain circumstances and order 47 provides the procedure therefor. 

22. Any person aggrieved by a decree or order may apply for a review of judgment, where no appeal is allowed or where an appeal is allowed but no appeal has been filed against such decree or order. "A person aggrieved" means a person who has suffered a legal grievance or against whom a decision has been pronounced which has wrongfully deprived of him something or wrongfully refused him something or wrongfully affected his title to something. In the case of MMB Catholicos Athanasius, AIR 1954 SC 526, it is held that application for review of a judgment may he made on any of the following grounds. 

i. Discovery of new and important matter or evidence, or, 
ii. mistake or error apparent on the fact of the record or, 

iii. any other sufficient reason. 

23. Now let us see whether the grounds shown by the petitioners are in consonance of the grounds shown in the above case. 

24. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order dated 13.04.1996. it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge frankly admitted that the plaintiff filed an application for amendment of plaint on 28.02.1987 under order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure to the effect that a Suit being No. 133 of 1916 was instituted for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession in respect of suit land which was finally decreed on compromise in terms of solenama filed by the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 Guljan Bibi. But the said application for amendment was fixed for hearing on 22.06.1987 and the same was again fixed on 24.06.1987 for hearing and order. The learned Subordinate Judge admitted in the impugned judgment that no order was passed on 24.06.1987 on amendment application and the matter of amendment was not included in the plaint. 

25. It is the contention of the plaintiffs petitioners that the petition for amendment was very much within the knowledge of the learned Subordinate Judge and if he had taken the application for amendment for consideration, the result of the suit would have been given in favour of the plaintiffs petitioners by virtue of amendment. 

26. It is admitted that the application for amendment which inadvertently escaped the notice of the Sub-ordinate Judge. This application for amendment is a important matter. A review is permissible on the discovery of such important matter of evidence', Therefore, where a review of a judgment is sought by a party on the grounds, discovery of such important and fresh evidence utmost care ought to be exercised by the court in granting it.

27. The tinder lying object of the provision of Rule 1 of order 47 is neither to enable the court to write a second judgment nor to give a second innings to the party who has lost the case because of his negligence or indifference. Therefore, a party seeking review must show that there was no remissness on his part. In the instant case, the plaintiffs petitioners had no negligence or !aches, it is the court itself which inadvertently failed to notice about the application for amendment. In this connection, the learned Advocate for plaintiffs petitioners refers the decision in the case of Azifa Khatun vs. Tulshi Ranjan Roy reported in 37 DLR 208 wherein their Lordships held that no wrong can go without a remedy and a suitor cannot be punished for the wrong done to him by the court itself. The plaintiffs petitioners cannot be suffered for the fault of court and in such situation remedy lies in the review. 

28. Another ground for review is a mistake or an error apparent on the face of the record. Considering the facts of this case, the error of the court is apparent on the face of the record. The error of the case is admitted which requires no explanation or argument to establish it. It would be suffice for us to say that where without any elaborate discussion one could infer such error. The facts of this case hold a clear case of error which is apparent on the face of the record. The pronouncement of judgment without taking into consideration the application of amendment which was fixed for hearing and order is clear error on the part of the court and the court should have reviewed the matter on the application of the plaintiffs petitioners but the court failed to do so. Thus the impugned judgment and order of rejection of review application is undoubtedly a erroneous one. 

29. The court manifestly committed wrong not considering the application for amendment. The court ought to have corrected it on review in order to do full and effective justice. It must be remembered that the power of review inheres in every court to prevent miscarriage of justice or to correct grave and palpable errors committed by it. 

30. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the review application on the wrong assumption that the plaint, solenama and order sheet of Title Suit No. 133 of 1916 is not allowable. Since the learned Sub-ordinate Judge mistakenly failed to notice the application for amendment that is why the learned Subordinate Judge fell on wrong conception that plaint, solenama and order sheet are not acceptable. Such erroneous assumption of material fact amounts to a error apparent on the face of the record calling for a review of the judgment. 
31. The learned Subordinate judge held that prayer for review is barred by limitation. In this connection the learned advocate for the petitioner referred the decision in the case Shawkat Ara Begum vs. Md. Wajuddin and others reported in 2 BLT(HCD) 226 that application for review by Article 173 of Limitation Act in which prescribed period is 90 days. But the learned Subordinate Judge wrongly held that the period of limitation is 30 days and calculating 30 days for limitation he illegally held that the review petition is barred by limitation. As the petitioners filed the review petition within 90 days and as such the petition is not barred by limitation. 

32. Though the scope of review under order 47, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure is very limited but non-consideration of amendment application which was before the court was a very important fact or evidence which resulted erroneous finding by the trial and such non-consideration of important fact clearly falls under the scope of review. This sort of review is necessary for the purpose of doing complete justice in a case, not for any academic purpose. The learned Subordinate Judge without applying the provision of order 47, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure passed the impugned judgment and decree. 

33. Since the plaintiffs petitioners succeeded to make out a case for review on the ground of discovery of important facts or new evidence which were cogent and sufficient causes for allowing review. As important matter of amendment was within the knowledge of the learned court which escaped his notice and such sort of mistakes could be corrected by the court on review. 
34. The right of review of a judgment is a substantive right. Review on the ground of discovery of important matter or evidence as referred to above confers the petitioners such a substantive right to review the judgment and such substantive right should not be ignored on the wrong assumption. 

35. Keeping in view the above provision of law, the revisional application merits consideration which must be succeeded. 

36. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost and the impugned judgment and order dated 13.04.1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Gazipur, in Review Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1995 rejecting the review petition and maintaining judgment and decree dated 13.02.1995 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge First Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 966 of 1985 dismissing the suit is set aside. The application for review is allowed and the learned Subordinate Judge is directed to consider the application of amendment as per provision of law and he is also directed to dispose of the case giving the parties opportunity to adduce evidence if any preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of records. 

37. Send down the L.C.R at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami   ------ For the Petitioner 
No one  ------ For the opposite party
parties:
Mrs. Sufia Khatoon   ------  Petitioner 
Versus 
The Mayor, Dhaka City Corporation and Others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Abdus Salam Mamun, J.: This Rule under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure was issued calling upon the opposite Party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 28.6.2001 passed by the Learned Additional District Judge, 2" Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 300 of 2000 should not be set aside and / or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 230/1995, 172/1999 in the court of the Learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka on praying for a declaration that the Defendant No. 1, the Dhaka City Corporation was not entitled to lease out the Scheduled land measuring an area of .023 ajutangsha under C. S. Plot No. 115 of Mouza Shahar Dhaka, Police Station Sutrapur, District, Dhaka to the respondent No. 3 or any other person and also that the Plot in question, i.e. C. S. 115 is contiguous to C. S. Plot No. 114 of which she is the owner and is in continuous possession of C. S. Plot No. 115 for the last 22 years. The Defendant Opposite Party No. 1 appeared in the suit by filing written statement and contested the same. The Learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka has after taking evidence dismissed the suit on 27.4.2000 and as against that order of dismissal the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 300 of 2000 before the Learned District Judge, Dhaka The appeal was ultimately transferred to the Court of the Learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for hearing . On 2.5.2001 the appellant filed a petition for temporary injunction against the respondents under Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a prayer for restraining the respondent No„ I from leasing out the suit land to the respondent No.3 or to any other person and also from dispossessing the plaintiff from the suit land. On 9.5.2001 the petition was taken up for hearing and the Learned Court has been pleased to pass an order directing the respondent Nos. 1-3 to show cause why they should not be restrained as prayed for within 10 days. On 14.5.2001 the respondent No. 1 appeared in the appeal and took an adjournment for filing Written Objection. On 28.5.2001 the appellant again filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for temporary injunction and pressing her pending petition. On 29.5.2000 this petition was taken up by the learned Court for hearing and the court has been pleased again to pass an order asking the respondents to show cause why temporary injunction should not be granted within 7 days. 

3. The appellant being aggrieved by the said order moved the Hon'ble High Court Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court under its revisional jurisdiction in Civil Revision No. 3263 of 2001 and on 25.6.2001 the Learned Court disposed of the said Civil Revision with a direction to the Appellate Court below to consider the matter of temporary injunction within two weeks from the date of receipt of the Order. On 10.6.2001 the respondent No. I has filed Written Objection to the injunction Petition. 

4. On the other hand, the respondent No. 1 has filed an application under Order 6 Rule 17 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying an amendment to its written objection on 26.6.2001. 

5. By order No. 16 dated 26.6.2001 the Learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court 
Dhaka has been pleased to reject the said application after hearing and holding that "the written objection was not a part of the pleadings and as such order 6 rule 17 was not applicable in such written objection" and also that Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure had made no provision for such amendment of a written objection and the Learned Advocate for the petitioner could not produce any authority from the Higher Courts and the mistake that was sought to be corrected by way of amendment was due to negligence of the concerned party and the negligent party was not entitled to relief," Annexur-A-2. 

6. Thereafter on 28.6.2001 the respondent No. 1 filed another application under Section 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the said Learned Court praying for said amendment of the written objection and the Learned Additional District Judge has been pleased to pass the impugned order on that application. 

7. From the impugned order No. 17 dated 28.6.2001 passed in Title Appeal 300 of 2000 it appears that the Learned Court has observed that the above date was not a fixed date of the appeal and that no copy of the application was served upon the appellant. The petition was taken up for hearing and the Learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka has been pleased to allow the petition holding that "the appellant side did not raise any objection to the petition by appearing in the court" and the 'for the purpose of determination of real facts in issue the same was allowed. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with this impugned order the Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioner has preferred this application before this Hon'ble court and obtained the present Rule. 

8. Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami, Learned Advocate has appeared for the petitioner and none appeared for the respondent No. 1 though the notice was duly served on 3.4.2002 on the opposite party No.1 . 

9. Mr. samarendra Nath Goswami has placing the application for revision together with Annexures submits that the proposed amendment that was sought to be made by application dated 26.6.2001 and rejected by order No. 16 dated 26.6.2001 and the amendment sought to be made by application dated 28.6.2001 and allowed by order No. 17 dated 28.6.2001 is substantially and factually same and the Learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka was not competent to allow the said proposed amendment which he had rejected two days ago. Mr. Goswami further submits that the Learned Additional District Judge, 2n-d Court, Dhaka has failed to assign any reason whatsoever to reverse his earlier order in the coluorable exercise of Section 153 and the same is without jurisdiction and liable to be set aside. 

10. Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami, the Learned Advocate has placed his reliance upon the case of Muzaffor Hossain Vs. Md. Shahidullah and others reported in 7 BLT (HCD) 1999 page 208. In similar Circumstances, their Lordships, in this case have held that "Finality must attach to a decision rendered by .a Court and the decision recorded by the said Court can be set aside or reversed not by the said Court but by the superior Court. The same court cannot sit on appeal on its own decision." Their Lordships have further been pleased to hold in this case that "No litigant got a right to get his affairs settled in the manner as he wishes. Every access to. justice should not be misused as a license to an untenable application. The arms of law cannot be stretched to untenable proceedings. If application of the present nature is allowed to go merrily and unchecked there will be no end of laying applications and applications after rejection and rejection of the applications and the litigant public with choose to settle the controversy in the same court without availing the remedy available by way of appeal and revision before the Higher Court. The law and procedure cannot be allowed to be eroded at the sweet wishes of the litigent public who attempts to get the controversy resolved in the manner he desires." 

11. Annexure - A to this revisional is the Written Objection submitted by the respondent No. 1 in the Court of the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 300 of 2000 opposing the application filed by the appellant-petitioner for injunction stating that the land in question, C. S. Plot No. 115 is contiguous land to the holding of the appellant and that the respondent No. 1 is using this land for dumping garbages and that the respondent No. 1 has not expressed its willingness to transfer this land in question to the respondent No. 3 or any other person and as such no cause of action arose for the application for injunction. This Written Objection was filed on 10.6.2001 but the petition under Order 6 Rule 17 was filed on 26.6.2001. In this application the respondent No. 1 has quoted the proposed amendment as follows: 

“প্রস্তাবিত সংশোধন”
(ক) লিখিত আপত্তির ১৩নং প্যারার শেষ লাইনের পরে নিম্ন বাক্যগুলি যথা-“ইহা উল্লেখ করা যাইতেছে যে, বিগত ইংরেজী ১৮/৩/২০০১ তারিখে জনাব সামসুদ্দিন আহমেদ বাবুল, পিতা হাজী সাহাবুদ্দিন আহমেদ, (জি,বি,এন সেকটার নং-৮) নং সাং-২৫, ফরাশগঞ্জ লেন, থানা-সুত্রাপুর, জেলা-ঢাকা একে ১নং রেসপনডেন্ট নালিশি সি,এস ১১৫ দাগে নালিশী ভূমিসহ একত্রে মোট ১৯২৫ বর্গফুট(এক হাজার নয়শত পঁচিশ বর্গফুট) ভূমি অস্থায়ী ব্যবহারের জন্য কতিপয় শর্তাধীনে অনুমতি প্রদান করিয়াছেন এবং ইহার খাস দখল ইংরেজী ২৮-৫-২০০১ তারিখে তাহার বরাবরে বুঝাইয়া দিয়াছেন। উক্ত সামসুদ্দিন আহমেদ বাবুল নিম্ন আদালতে মুল দেওয়ানী মোকাদ্দমায় এবং অত্র আদালতে অত্র আপীল ও পক্ষভুক্ত নহে।” সংযোজন হইবে।
12. On hearing of this application the learned Appellate Court below has rightly held that Order 6 Rule 17 was not available to a person for whose latches the alleged mistake took place. This Order was a final order to the extent of the proposed amendment was concerned disposing the petition and the matter on merit This order was a revisable order under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and this remedy was opened to the respondent No. 1 but for reasons best known to him the respondent No. 1 did not resorted to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh but found it convenient to file a petition before the same court under Section 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking the same amendment before the same Judge and by the impugned order the learned Additional District Judge , 2"d Court, Dhaka has entertained the petition and allowed the amendment. 

Section 153 of the Civil Procedure Court reads as follows : 
"153- The Court may at any time, and on such terms as to costs or otherwise as it may think fit, amend any defect or error in any proceeding in a suit; and all necessary amendments shall be made for the purpose of determining the real question or issue raised by or depending on such proceeding". 

13. The rudiment of the Section is that the defect or error that is to be amended was not due to any latches of the parties in the proceeding. In a suit may be that the Court on its own accord finds any defect or error in a proceeding which may vitiate the proceeding if not amended. In that case this Section 153 is available to the Court concerned. It is not an alternative remedy of Order 6 rule 17 of the Civil procedure Code. 

14. This Section 153 has undergone judicial scrutiny and in the Case of Sachindra Chandra Chakravarti Vs. Jnanendra Narayan Singh Roy and another, reported in AIR 1963 Calcutta 417 their Lordships held that "Section 153 cannot be invoked by a party who is guilty of latches to cover up his default. The powers thereunder can be exercised by the Court in a case where the defect or error which would vitiate the proceeding is not due to a party's default. A negligent party cannot ask the Court to overlook his aches and rectify defect." 

15. It is rule of prudence that whenever court holds anything in a proceeding incompatible what it held earlier must assign sufficient reasons for making the departure and holding otherwise. When the Order attaches finality to the matter the Court becomes functus Officio as soon as the order is passed in so far that particular matter concerned and particular order in question becomes subject matter of the Appellate or revisional Courts. 
In the instant case the learned Court found that a Written Objection filed against a application for injunction is not part pleading but subsequently deviated from this point when it became functus official in respect of proposed amendment. 
Admittedly, the petitioner is a holder c neighboring C.S. Plot No.114 and the respondent No. 1 was using the contiguous land under C.S. Plot No. 115 for dumping garbages causing various inconveniences to the petitioner. The respondent No. 1 has file Written Statement in the suit denying that was trying to transfer the suit land to the respondent No. 3 or any other person also stating the same in the Written Objection t the application for injunction that it was not even thinking for transfer of it to the respondent No. 3 or any other person but after 16 days it has come to say by incorporating an amendment that it has given permission or Licence to the respondent No. 3 to use the land on certain conditions on 18.3.2001 any handed over possession on 28.5.2001. This subsequent version has changed nature any character of the suit. It is not open to a Cow under section 153 to allow an amendment, which will alter the real matter in controversy between the parties and involve setting up a new case. (Kand Vs. Waghow, 3DLR (PC) 310). This suit was instituted in the year 1995 and the allege transaction which was the subject matter of proposed amendment is hit by the Doctrine of Lis pendence under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act. In the Case of Hochenaddi SK.Vs Esmail Sikdar, 9 DLR 294 it was held that "the possession which a party to the said obtains during the pendency of the suit instituted by the Plaintiff cannot alter the rights of the parties in the suit, for those must be deter-mined according to the position prevailing on the date of the institution of the suit.
" It is also well know that the appeal is continuation of suit. This is again hit by the principle enunciated by the judiciary that "what can not be done directly, cannot be done indirectly;" that is, what cannot be transferred by way of lease cannot be transferred by way of permission or License. The person who is enduring ordour of garbages has got some sort of precedence in respect of garbage land when the question of third party is concerned. 

16. The impugned order 17 date 28.6.2001 passed by Mr. Mohammed Kader Newaz, Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 300 of 2000 has no leg to stand. It is therefore, set aside. 

17. Mr. Samarendra Nath Goswami has submitted lack of his instruction about the direction given by this Hon'ble Court to the Additional District Judge, 2" Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 3263 of 2001 to dispose of the injunction matter within two weeks from the date of receipt of that order. The Learned Additional District Judge, 2"d Court, Dhaka is hereby directed to dispose of the appeal on merit, preferable within six weeks from the date of receipt of this order, Stay granted earlier is hereby vacated. 

18. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Mazibar Rahman, Advocate  ------  For the Petitioner.
Mr. Kazi Shafiqul Hasan, Advocate  ------  For the Opposite Party Nos. 1 & 2.
parties:
Md. Ali & Ors.  ------  Petitioners. 
Versus 
Md. Aminuddin & Ors.  ------  Oppo. Parties.
full_judgment:
Mr. A.B.M. Khairul Haque, J. : This is an application for Review of the judgment and order passed on 5.12.2001 discharging the Rule.

2. The petitioner and the Opposite Party Nos. 3 and 4 as plaintiffs filed a suit being Title Suit No. 90 of 1993 praying for a declaration that the deed of gift dated 17.3.1983 as described in Kha Schedule to the plaint in respect of the gifted land is false, fraudulent, collusive and without any consideration and it is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The Trial Court decreed the suit while Appellate Court allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit on the grounds inter alia that the date of knowledge of the alleged deed of gift dated 17.3.1983 was neither stated in the plaint nor proved by any evidence on behalf of the plaintiffs. On this finding the appeal was allowed and the suit was dismissed. Against this judgment and order, a civil revision being Civil Revision No. 4745 of 2000 was filed. The revisional application as taken up for hearing on 5.12.2001 and although the learned Advocate for the petitioner was present but none appears on behalf of the opposite party. After hearing, the rule was discharged on the ground that the last Court of fact rightly found that the plaintiffs failed to prove the date of knowledge by adducing proper evidence.

3. In this petition for review, Mr. Mazibar Rahman, Advocate, appears for the petitioner while, Mr. Kazi Shafiqul Hasan, Advocate, appears on behalf of the opposite parties.

 4. Mr. Mazibar Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that since both the Appellate Court as well as the Revisional Court committed an error apparent on the face of the record in holding that the plaintiffs did neither assert their date of knowledge either in the plaint or in the deposition, the date of their knowledge of the deed in dispute was not proved, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. This being an error on the face of the record, it comes within the ambit of XLVII Rule 1, of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned Advocate submits that the review petition is maintainable and his revisional application should be heard afresh because non-consideration of the plaint and also the evidence in its proper perspective specially paragraph 4 of the plaint and the depositions of P.W. 1 him-self and also Ext. 10, an order passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), high-lighting the date of knowledge of the plain-tiffs. In support of his contention the learned Advocate cites the decisions reported in AIR 1964 All 516, AIR 1986 Born 308, 49 DLR 437, 1999 (VII) BLT AD 151. 

5. On the other hand Mr. Kazi Shafiqul Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submits that the scope of review is very limited and the issue of knowledge being decided concurrently both by the Appellate Court as well as the Revisional Court it cannot be reopened, that the instant review petition does not come within four corners of Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. As such, he prays for dismissal of review petition. In support of his contention the learned Advocate cites the decision reported in 49 DLR AD 108. 

6. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the application for review, the plaint, the Ext. 10 and also the oral deposition of P.W. 1. It is apparent on the face of the record that the learned Additional District Judge made an error in appreciating the evidence while holding that the plaintiffs failed to state in their plaint as well as in the evidence the date of their knowledge about the deed in question. As a matter of fact, it is specifically so stated in the plaint and also in the deposition of P.W. 1 about their date of knowledge of the deed in question. As such the finding of the Appellate Court below, the last court of fact, as well as this court in its revisional jurisdiction were wrong in holding that the plaintiffs failed to disclose their date of knowledge. Since the error is apparent it comes within the ambit of Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. As such, the review petition has got merit and should be allowed. 

7. Since this court, in its revisional jurisdiction, discharged the rule only on the issue of limitation, for ends of justice, both the parties should be allowed to agitate all the other issues involved in the suit as well as in the appeal.

 8. In the result, this petition for review is allowed and the rule is restored to its original file and number for further hearing on all the other relevant issues.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Munsur Habib  ------ for the petitioner.

parties:
Md. Abdul Karim Khan  ------ Petitioner.
Versus
Md. Abdul Hamid Gayeen and others, ------ Opposite parties.
full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Muhammad Dastagir Hussain  J:This Rule arises as against the judgment and decree dated 5th August, 1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat Rajshahi in Title Appeal No. 27 of 1992 reversing the judgment and decree dated 29th November, 1993 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mohanpur Thana Rajshahi it other class suit No. 34 of 1990. 

2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted suit for restoration after declaring the right title interest of the suit land mentioned in the schedule of the plaint being other class suit No. 34 of 1990 in the court of Assistant Judge, Mohanpur Upazilla, Rajshahi and further case of the plaintiff is that the suit land mentioned in the schedule belonged to the petitioner and the petitioner was in need of money . and proposed the defendant No. 1 for taking loan of Tk. 1500/- after mortgaging the suit land to the defendant No. 1 The defendant No. 1 accepted the proposal and after receiving Tk. 1500/- the plaintiff executed a deed of sale in favour of the defendant No. 1 and registered on 18th December, 1969 and the defendant No. 1 also executed and registered a deed of reconveyance on the same date and delivered possession there of in favour of the defendant No. 1. The plaintiff requested the defendant No.1 to recovery the land in favour of the plaintiff but he failed to recovery the same on different pretexts and finally on the 30th December, 1989 refused to recovery the suit land in favour of the plaintiff and as such the plaintiff was constrained to file the suit on 20th May, 1990. 

3. The Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegation to the plaint and asserted that since the plaintiff did not repay the mortgage money amounting to Tk. 1500/- he is not entitled to get any decree in the suit. 

4. The defendant No. 2 and 3 filed a joint written statement stating inter alia that the defendant No. 1 purchased the suit land from the plaintiff and while possessing the same R.S. record was prepared in his name and on requirement of money the defendant No.1 transferred 21 decimals of land in favour of the defendant No.2 and 3 by a registered kabala No. 1953/87 dated 18.3.1987 and delivered possession thereof in favour of them and since they were possessing the same and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

5. The plaintiff adduced 4 witnesses and the defendant adduced 8 witnesses to prove their respective cases and after hearing the parties and the Exibts. The trial court found 
that the trans action was out and out Usufructury Mortgage and after lapse of 7 years, the defendant No. 1 was bound to reconvey the land free from encumbrance under section 95A of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act, That being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court the defendants preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge and on transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Rajshahi who has' allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment of the trial court in relying a decision reported in 3 B. L. T. 141 (AD) holding that the plaintiff is not entitled to get any decree as per section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

6. The terms and condition as stipulated in the Ekrarnama which are as follows. 
“ বাদী বাংলা ১২৭৬ সালের ৩১শে চৈত্র তারিখের মধ্যে বিক্রয় কবলা দলিলের মূল্যের টাকা ফেরত দিলে ১লা বিবাদী নালিশী সম্পত্তি বাবদ বাদীর বরাবর বিক্রয় কবলা দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রি করিয়া দিবেন।

7. Mr. Munsur Habib the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner submits that the learned court of appeal below. has misconstrued section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act reads as follows : 
95A Treatment of certain transaction as usufructuary mortgage Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof where the transfer or receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to posses and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share there of for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall not withstanding any-thing contained in the document relating to the transfer. Be deemed to be 11 BLT (HCD) 20 
a complete usufrucuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

8. Therefore, be submits that the deed of sale was executed on 18.12.69 and the krarnama was also executed and registered on the same date being 18.12.69 stipulating terms and conditions that after 7 years he would get back his property. According to Limitation Act period is 60 years. The plaintiff after lapse of 7 years instituted the suit on 20th May 1990, which is written the period of limitation. Therefore the learned court of appeal below while reversing the 
decision of the trial court did not consider this aspect and has allowed the appeal which occasioned failure of justice requires to be interfered by this court. 

9. Mr. Waziullah alOngwith Mrs. Amatul Karim the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party could not substantiate their argument in view of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

10. Since the petitioner invokes Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act that after enjoyment of the usufruct for maximum period of 7 years he is entitled to get back his property and the suit having been filed on 20.5.1990. is within the period of limitation. Therefore, the cited . decision reported in 3 B.L.T. (AD) 141 has got no application in this particular case as the transaction is construed to be a mortgage for a period of 7 years. The transaction was alive and subsisting on the date of promulgation of P.0.88 of 1972 i.e. on 3.8.72. 

11. I find substance in this Rule. Accordingly the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, and Artha Rin Adalat, Rajshahi in Title Appeal No. 27 of 1994 is set aside. 

12. Send down the lower court, records at once. 

End.

lawyer:

Versus
The Commissioner of Customs, Customs House, Dhaka and others  ------  Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Abdus Salam Mamun,  J. : 'This Rule Nisi was issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents to show cause, why Memo No. 5-12 Cus(175) Group-5/Forgery/01/6357 dated 26.8.2001 issued by the respondent No. 1 in reference to the Memo No. 05/07 (114) Gopa/ Go 0 Ta/2001/724 dated 25.7.2001 issued by the Respondent No.. 2 demanding an amount of TK. 2,14.50,715/- against the petitioner and stopping clearance of the imports of the petitioner (Annexure--B- and  B-1) should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be no legal effect.

2. Facts of this Writ Petition, in short, are that the petitioner-company is a 100% export oriented Garments Industry enjoying the Bonded Warehouse facilities under Bond Licence and has been carrying on business since incorporation in 1984. In the year 2001 she received a Master L.0 being No. 82002248 dated 7.6.2001 for an amount of US$665,878.00 from the account of one BERNE APPAREL, USA through the Bank OEN, N. A Chicago, Illinois, USA for supply of ready-made Garments under authorization of transfer by one Aquarian's (USA) and the stipulated time limit for shipments were up to 15.9.2001. 

3. The petitioner has imported and released through the customs about 76% of required fabrics and accessories free of customs duties and taxes under the law under several back to back L/Cs and used the same in the factory for manufacturing and exporting readymade garments. Thereafter, she opened back to back L/C No. RAM 0101 DP 330 dated 2.7.2001 for an amount of US$ 79,635.00 for import of fabrics and accessories as per pro-forma invoice and on arrival of the said goods at the Zia International Airport under Air way Bill No. 696108 67850 corresponding to Master Airway Bill No. 82315575 made an endorsement through her clearing agent on 13.8.2001 for clearing the consignment. But the respondent No.1 has verbally refused to deliver her Pass Book on the allegations that they have received complain against her of evasion of duty. 

4. The petitioner then filed an application to the Commissioner of Customs. It is inconceivable why and under what law and authority the Customs officials shall send recommendations of the investigation authority, a confidential communication, to a person against whom allegations of violation of law and evasion of customs duties have been prima facie proved in an investigation made by the competent authority in accordance with law. 

18. The Maxim audi alterem partem- none be condemned unheard'- is also applicable in the administrative and business arena and the petitioner in the instant case was entitled to a show-cause notice against the allegations brought against her and in our view, she was also entitled to get a legible copy of the investigation report but under no circumstances the respondent No. I was authorized to sent or the petitioner was entitled to receive the confidential communication containing recommendations on the basis of investigation, made by an investigation Directorate and communicated to the recipient under confidential cover; Apart from the principle of Natural Justice, the Section 32 of the Customs Act, 1969 has expressly provided for issuing show-cause notice to the person who has made untrue statement, declaration 
etc. and as such. issuing a show-cause notice was the statutory obligation on the part of the Customs Officials and getting the same was a legal right of the person concerned so that she can make an effective representation to the allegations brought against her. The Customs proceeding is a quasijudicial proceeding where the authority concerned is bound by law, especially, by the provisions of the Customs Act, 1969. 
19. The learned Assistant Attorney-General placing her reliance upon the case of Chairman, National Board of Revenue Vs. Nasrin Banu and 5 others, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 171 submits that the Annuxure-B-1 has neither been communicated to the petitioner nor has it created any right in her favour. It was held in this case, that "Interministerial / Divisional communications made in the process of reaching a decision excommunicated to the affected person, do not create a legal right in their favour". 

The learned Assistant Attorney-General submits that the Annexure-B-1 was written by the Director-General of the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate and sent to the Commissioner, Customs House, Dhaka under confidential classification and process. It is an internal communication. 

In the case of Bangaldesh Vs . Dhaka Steel Works Ltd., reported in 45 DLR (AD) 69, their Lordships held that "Internal exercises of the Government communicated to the concerned person are not enforceable. No legal right can be founded on the nothing done by the Government and furnished in the Writ Petition". Similar view has also been taken in the case of Al-Haj Abul Basher Vs. Bangladesh, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 11 that inter-Ministerial Communications do not create any legal right in favour of any person.

 20. Mrs. Nahid Mahtab, the Learned Assistant Attorney -General relying upon the case of Shawn Apparels Ltd. Vs. Commissioner of Customs and others, reported in 52 DLR 316 submits that if the contention of the petitioner is accepted, for argument's sake, that the Annexure-B-1 was communicated to her by the Customs Official, in that case, the concerned Customs Official shall be responsible for unauthorised or illegal actions and activities and the Government can not be held responsible. 
In this case, their Lordships have held that "For illegal and unauthorised actions of the Government officials, Government can not be held responsible."
We find substance in the submissions of the Learned Assistant Attorney-General and hold that the responsibility in this case, is not of the Government but of the concerned Customs Officials. The Annexure-B-1 has got no enforceability in law and no cause of action for filing this Writ Petition arose out of Annexure-B-1.
21. The Annexure-B, in substance, is a show-cause notice though due to lack of application of Judicial mind the concerned Customs official has asked the petitioner, by this Annexure, to submit an "explanatory reply" without mentioning any time limit. But by no stretch of imagination the Annexure-B could- be said to be a Demand Notice demanding any amount of money from the petitioner. We therefore, find no substance in the contentions of the petitioner that the Annexure-B is a Demand Notice' demanding money from her. 

22. A show-cause notice does not violate any of the fundamental rights guaranteed to citizen by the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and as such no Writ Petition is maintainable against a show cause notice. 

23. Chapter XI of he Customs Act, 1969 has provided for Ware housing of goods under Licence and expressed provisions are there in this respect. There is a S. R. 0. No. 153 —Law/ 93/1520/Cus dated 3.8.1993 called “সম্পূর্ন রপ্তানীমুখী শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠান( সাময়িক আমদানী) বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৩।” এই বিধিমালার ২য় তপশীলে ইউটিলাইজেশন ডিক্লাবেশনের ৰিধানাবলী এবং শর্তাবলী লিপিবদ্ধ আছে বর্তমান রীট আবেদনকারী এই বিধানাবলী অনুযায়ী শুল্ককর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট প্রতিশ্রুতি প্রদান করেছেন যে "আমি আমরা (বন্ডার) আরো প্রতিশ্রুতি প্রদান করিতেছি যে, যদি ঊপরিউক্ত ইউটিলইিজেশন ডিক্লারেশন (ইউ,ডি) এ কোন মি্থ্যা ঘোষণা, অসত্য তথ্য, অযৌক্তিক সহগ, বিবরণী ইত্যাদি পাওয়া
যায় অখবা ঋণপত্রে নির্ধারিত সময়সীমা বা ঋণপত্রে বর্ধিত্ সময়সীমা বা শুল্ক আইন, ১৯৬৯ এর ৯৮ ধারায় নির্ধারিত
সময়সীমার মধ্যে (যাহা পূর্ববর্তী হয়) উপরিউক্ত ইউটিলইিজেশন (ইউ, ভি) এ উল্লিখিত পরিমান আমদানীকৃত
কাঁচামাল দ্বারা তৈরী পোষাক রপ্তানী করিয়া রপ্তানীর সপক্ষে সংশ্লিষ্ট শিপিং ডকুমেন্টস এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট লিয়েন ব্যাংকের প্রসিড:
রিয়েলাইজেশন সার্টিফিকেট (PRC) দাখিল করিতে না পারি তবে আমদানীকৃত কাঁচামালের উপর প্রদেয় শুল্ক, মুসক
ইত্যাদিসহ কালেকটর কর্তৃক আরোপিত জরিমানা ও নিরুপিত্ সুদ প্রদান করিতে উক্ত শুল্ক আইন, বিদ্যমান অন্যান্য আইনে
আওতায় কোন আইনগত পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করা হইলে তাহা মানিয়া লইতে বাধ্য থাকিব ৷"

24.In this undertaking the petitioner h herself undertaken not to make any false declaration, untrue statement, accounts el and also to produce and furnish relevant shipping documents, proceeds realization certificate (PRC) from the Lien bank support of export of readymade garment made of imported raw materials to the Customs authority, or else, to face the leg consequences. The petitioner can not make a subsequence departure from her undertaking on the plead that the documents are already lying with the Customs authority and she is not bound furnish/produce those documents or reply show-cause notice as required by the Custom authority in Annexure-B. 
The petitioner, in this Writ petition urging upon this Court to presume correctness of her documents annexed with the Writ petition, Supplementary Affidavit al Affidavit-in reply which the respondent No has alleged to have been prima facie foul forged and fabricated.  Section 211 states that the petitioner shy preserve these documents to furnish to Customs officer whenever required within years (earlier it was 5 years).
 
In her Utilization Declaration she undertook to produce these documents to the Customs Officials. She is therefore bound by law and Licence. This Court shall not make any presumption on disputed annexures or facts. 

25. Annexure-H to the Writ petition is a Letter written by the  petitioner to the Commissioner of Customs, Dhaka on 27.8.2001 praying a legible copy of the Investigation Report and release of her consignment in hand. On the prayer of the petitioner we have called for the concerned office record from the Customs authority, Dhaka to be produced through the office of the Learned Attorney General for Bangladesh and the Customs authority has produced the same. On perusal of the record, we find that the Customs authority has received the said application of the petitioner, praying a legible copy of the investigation report, on 28.8.2001 but managed to sleep over it without supplying a legible copy or giving any reply to the petitioner. The Customs authority, as we find, found room to write so many notes and orders in the note-sheets of their record but could not make room within this long span of time to give a reply to an importer and exporter who is also contributing to the economy of the county. It is surprising to note that though the confidential recommendations dated 25.7.2001 of the Director General Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate in its item No. (01) contained a recommendation to take penal actions against the concerned. Customs Officials/employees after enquiry, the note-sheets of the record show that the Customs authority did not take any step whatsoever for enquiry and action against its. Officers/ employees in accordance with the findings and recommendations of the Investigation Directorate. 

26. Had the Commissioner of Customs, Dhaka specifically mentioned on the Annexure-B to the Writ Petition to be a "Show -cause notice" asking the petitioner to showcause within a given time-frame, i. e, reasonable time, and supplied a legible copy of the investigation report, as was prayed for, the situation and circumstances, in this case, could have been otherwise and the proceeding for recovery of the Government revenue could not be prolonged and impeded. The Commissioner of Customs is an adjudicating/ appellate authority under the Customs Act, 1969 and as such expected to comply with the provisions of the Customs Act in the first place and first of all in performing his function and failure to do so is incompatible to his office and responsibility. We strongly disapprove such conduct of a responsible office holder. Transparency of the decision making bodies have been repeatedly emphasized by this Court. In the Case of Hundai Corporation Vs. Sumukin B. Corporation and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 88 their Lordships held that "transparency in the policy/ decision making as well as in the functioning of public bodies is desired for more than one reason and particularly in the matter where financial 
interest of the State is involved. " So also in the Case of ETV Vs. Bangladesh and others, reported in 10 BLT (AD) 108. 

27. Under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the High Court Division may, on the application of any person aggrieved, declare any act done or proceeding taken by a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a Local authority has been done or taken without lawful authority and is of no Legal effect. 

The Commissioner of Customs is a lawful authority, under the Customs Act, 1969 to take a proceeding against a person against whom allegations have been received from the competent authority of violation of provision of the Customs Act, 1969 and evasion of Customs duties. Article 102 of the Constitution is not available to such a person against such a show cause notice.

28. It is worthy to note that the petitioner in paragraph II of her Writ petition has stated that stated that : "Respondent No.1 has merely made allegations against the petitioner and the petitioner is due to reply the-same. Unless and until the adjudication process initiated by the Customs authorities culminates after the due process in a finding and decision that duties, etc. are payable by the petitioner no such demand may be made." 
As we find that no such demand of payment of money has yet beeil made by the respondent from the petitioner. she is at liberty to give reply to the show-cause notice on receipt of a copy of the investigation report. The respondents are directed to supply a legible copy of the investigation report to the petitioner forthwith. Stay granted earlier is hereby vacated. 

29. We therefore, accept the submissions of the Learned Assistant Attorney-General that the Writ petition is pre-matured involving disputed questions of facts and not maintainable but find it expedient to send a copy of this Judgment to the Chairman, National Board of Revenue, Dhaka to prevent further perils. 

30. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any, order as to costs. Let a copy of this Judgment be sent to the Chairman, National Board of Revenue, Dhaka as aforesaid. Send down the Customs record. 

End.
