33. The decision in the case of Re Anath Bandhu Guha and sons Ltd. (1957) 7PLR Dhaka series 159, arose on an application for leave to appeal to the Federal Court out of a petition under Section 38 of the Companies Act, 1913, praying for rectification of the register of the company, which was allowed by a Bench of the High Court and Upheld in appeal by a Division Bench, In refusing to give certificate, Amin Ahmed, C. J., held as the Companies Act, 1862, Lord Coleridge, follows: 

 ------ We have no doubt that the provision of section of the Campanies Act are very wide, and in appropriate cases give a Judge dealing with Company matters a very wide discretion in granting speedy relief to the holder of shares,   under section 38 the Court has ample scope and power to grant relief and save the parties from being harassed and unnecessarily relegated to protracted litigation in a simple case." 
Since the said decision, the legal position in this respect has been settled.
As a matter of fact, this principle was settled even long before Anath Bandhu Guha's case. In the case of re London, Hamburgh, and Continental Exchange Bank (Ward and Henry's case) (1867) 2Ch. A 431, where the question, inter alia was as to the extent of jurisdiction given to the Court under Section 35 of the Companies Act, 1862, Sir, G. J. Turner, L. J., held as follows: 
"The intention of the section, as I understand it, is to provide a summary means of dealing with cases which the Court in its discretion should think might be so dealt with. A large and wide discretion ought, I think, to be exercised by the Court in determining whether it will exercise the power given to it by the section, and it is, I think, too narrow a construction to hold that the section applies only where there is error, mistake, or default, on the part of the company." 
In the Matter of The Diamond Roch Boring Company Limited, Ex. Parte, A. R. Shaw (1877)2QBd 463, on the question of jurisdiction of the Court under Section 35 of 
C.J. Held as follows. 
"Looking at all the words of s. 35, and giving them a reasonable construction, I think that the legislature intended to give the Court jurisdiction to make an order so as to decide questions of title, trusting to the discretion of the Court not to decide in this summary manner any intricate or difficult question of title, but that, if the Court think fit, they have jurisdiction to make the order in all cases." 
Again, in the case of Ramesh Chandra Mitter Vs. Jogini Mohan Chatterji (1920)ILR 47 Cal. 901, where a mortgagee of the uncalled capital of the shares raised objection to the prayer of a share-holder, to remove his name from the register of the company under section 38 of the Companies Act, Mookerjee and Fletcher, JJ. held as follows. 
"It is now well settled that although persons are not entitled to an order ex debito justitiae, the jurisdiction under section 38 is unlimited, with a discretion in the Court in the circumstances of each case   In a simple case where an immediate rectification is essential, it may be desirable to apply under the section. but if the case is at all complicated, an action should be brought. The respondent has, however, argued that section 38 does not authorize the Court to consider a dispute between a member and a stranger, In support of this proposition, reliance had been placed upon the language of sub section (3) of section 38 which is in these terms: "On any application under this section, the Court may decide any question relating to the title of any person who is a party to the application to have his name entered in or omitted from the register, whether the question arises between members or alleged members, or between members or alleged members on the one hand and the Company on the other hand: and generally, may decide any question necessary or expedient to be decided for rectification of the register," Mr. Ghose has contended that the generality of the concluding words of the sub-section is materially restricted by what precedes, and that notwithstanding their comprehensive phraseology, we are bound to hold that, "a question necessary or expedient to be decided for rectification of the register" must be a question between members or alleged members, or between member on the one hand and the Company on the other hand. We are of opinion that we should not adopt this narrow interpretation of the section. The Legislature obviously intended that the Court should have the widest possible power to determine, in its discretion, questions which may appear to it to be necessary or expedient for decision before an order for rectification is made or refused." 

This decision has been upheld and reiterated in many a subsequent decisions. In the case of Haque Brothers Vs. Shamsul Haque 39 DLR (1987) 290, a Division Bench held as follows. 
"The jurisdiction conferred on company court under section 38 is very wide and unlimited though it is a direction to grant or refuse such relief. We do not find that the Company Judge has acted illegally in allowing such relief under section 38 of the Companies Act in the facts of the present case. Section 38 of our Companies Act is equivalent to section 155 of Indian Companies Act. In section 155 of the Indian Act, "the name of any person is fraudulently inserted or omitted has been omitted; whereas in section 38 of the Companies Act it has been retained. Thus the scope of Section 38 of the Act is very wide and the Company Judge has rightly passed the order of rectification of share Registers of the Companies." 
But in the case of United Planters Vs. Moshatraf Hossain 34 DLR(1982)345 while unholding the wide power of the Court, M. H. Rahman, J. (as his Lordship then was) found in that case that the moot question was not whether it involved a complicated question of title but whether the application was, within the purview of Section 38 of the Act and since the relief prayed for did not come within the ambit of Section 38 of the Act, the petition was dismissed. 
However, the decisions in the case of Haque Brothers Vs. Shamsul Haque 39 DLR(1987)290 and United Chemicals and Pharmaceuticals Ltd. Vs. Niranjan Dey 47 DLR(1995) 423, held although in obiter, that the scope of Section 38 (of Companies Act, 1913) is wider than the Indian provision contained in Section 155 of Companies Act of 1956 (of India) where one of the earlier ground of rectification, which is, 'The name of any person fraudulently inserted or omitted, has been omitted.
Since same kind of omission has been made in Section 43 of the Companies Act, 1994, Mr. Rafique-ul-Huq, argued that in contradistinction and in suppression of the provision of Section 38, the Court cannot now under Section 43, exercise its jurisdiction for rectification of share register if there is any allegation of fraud. 
This argument although attractive but not correct.
In India, the Indian Companies Act, 1956, was enacted, repealing the earlier Companies Act, 1913. The power of the Court to rectify the register of members was provided under Section 38 of the Act of 1913 so also in Section 155 of the Companies Act, 1956. But inspite of omission in the said provision as referred to above, the power of the Court in direction rectification was not at all narrowed down. The Supreme Court of India, in the case. of Harinagar Sugar Mills Vs. Shyarn Sunder AIR 1961 SC 1669 referred to both the provisions in this manner at para-I0. 
"The power given to the court under S. 38 is now confirmed with slight modification by S. 155 of the Companies Act, 1956. Under that section, the court may rectify the register of shareholders if the name of any person is without sufficient entered cause in or omitted from the register of members of a company, or default is made, or unnecessary delay has taken place in entering on the register the fact of any person having ceased to be member. The Court is in exercising this jurisdiction competent to decide any question relating to the title of the person claming to have his name registered and generally to decide all questions which may be necessary or expedient to decide for the rectification." 
In the meantime, the Companies Act, 1956 (of India) under went further amendment. Section 155 itself have been repeated and assimilated in the amended Section 111, by an amendment Act of 1988, with effect from 31st May, 1991. The provision as to the power of the Court to rectify register of members is now contained in Section 111(4) of the Companies Act. 1956 (of India). 
Again, the Supreme Court of India, however, in the case of Public Passenger Service Ltd. Vs. M. A. Khadar AIR 1966 SC 489=36 Comp. Cas I SC observed as follows.
 "---- Where by reason of its complexity or otherwise the matter can more conveniently be decided in a suit, the court may refuse leave under S. 155 of the Act and relegate the parties to a suit." 
In the case of Gulabrai Kalidas Naik V. Lazhidas Lallubha i Patel of Baroda (1978) 48 Corn Cas 438(Guj, Desai, J. held as follows as page 456: 
"Therefore, both on principle and on authority, it becomes crystal clear that a petition under section 155 cannot straightaway be disposed of by merely saying that as complex and complicated question of title are raised, the matter ought to decided by way of a suit and the party ought to be relegated to a suit. At best, it can be said that the question is addressed to the direction of the court and if the court exercises direction one way, namely, to undertake to hear the petitions is decision cannot said to be one without jurisdiction." 
In the case of Ammonia Supplies Corporation Private Ltd. Vs. Modern Plastic Containers (Pvt.) Ltd. AIR 1994 Delhi 51, the Full Bench of the Delhi High Court held as follows at para-21. 
"The object of S. 155, in our view, is to provide remedy in non controversial matters or in matters where a quick decision is necessary and can be rendered in order to obviate irreparable injury to a party. Section 155, is ordinarily not intended of settling controversies necessitating a regular investigation and in such cases the Company Court can decline to entertain petitions in exercise of its discretionary power and say that since serious disputes are involved, the proper forum for their adjudication is a civil court S. 155(3) only shows that question relating to title can also be examined by the Company Court but that is also possible without detailed examination of complicated questions of fact and law, requiring extensive oral and documentary evidence and it cannot be inferred from S. 155(3) that the remedy is not summary. It would depend on facts of each case. It is not necessary in every case where the question relating to title may be involved that there has to be a detailed examination and determination of oral and documentary evidence. The question is not whether the company Court has no jurisdiction but is that can the court in its discretion decline to exercise it where disputed and complicated questions are involved requiring examination of extensive oral and documentary evidence. We do not think that a respondent would be able to oust the jurisdicion of the company Court by a mere assertion in the reply about fraud orforgery or want of condiseration. In such a case the Company Court can and certainly would examine whether the said assertion is being made only with a view to oust the jurisdiction of the company Court or assertions are such which would require detailed examination of the evidence. In the former case the Company Court would proceed with the adjudication of a petition under S. 155 In the later case the Company Court would be justified in exercise of its discretion to reject the petition and relegate the parties to a regular civil suit. It has to be borne in mind that the power to rectify the register of members is discretionary and so also the power to decide questions relating to title as is apparent from bare reading of sub sec. (3) of S. 155 of the Act." 

34. It appears that the Court under Section 43 of the Companies Act, 1994, no doubt exercises summary jurisdiction but of very wide amplitude. An allegation of fraud or forgery, even if it is correct would not necessarily take away the jurisdiction of the Court. The omission of one of the grounds of rectification, under Section 43, as it used to be under Section 38 of the Companies Act, 1913, such as the name of any person is fraudulently entered in or omitted, does not narrow down the wide discretion of the Court in deciding even complicated questions of fact. 
It would therefore appear that the jurisdiction of the Court under Section 38 of the earlier Act of 1913 does not suffer any change under Section 43 of the present Act. 35. So far the issue of the disputed questions of fact are concerned, there is hardly any petition where some of the facts are not disputed. If is also to be noted that the petitioners are not entitled to an order ex debito justitiae. It would depend on the facts of each case. It the facts as presented before the Court are complicated, still the Court may proceed to decide the matter provided it is possible to do so on the basis of papers and documents before it but if the Court finds that the allegations and disputes among the parties are of such a serious nature that adjudication of the matter in accordance with law requires extensive examination of both oral and documentary evidence, in such a case the Court may refuse to exercise its discretionary power under Section 43 but leave the parties to settle their dispute before a Civil Court. 

36. In that view of the matter, I agree with the view of Dr. Zahir that Anath Bandhu Guhs's case still holds the field so far the powers of the Court in rectification of the register of members are concerned.
37. Mr. Mustafizur Rahman, Advocate, also appeared on behalf of the respondent no. 17. He submitted that out of the total number of 37 share-holders seven of them responded but only partial payments which shoe the required notices were duly issued and served upon all the rest of the share-holders also He further submitted that the shares were issued not for any collateral purpose but for survival of the company because the suit for eviction was hanging upon the respondent-company, filed by its land lord threatening its eviction from the premises which would obviously resulted in the closure of the hospital leading to the ultimate winding up of the company that only in order to save the respondent-company from sah an eventuality, the management of the respondent-company. which includes both the respondent no. 17 and also Dr. Ruhul Amin, to move quickly in order to mobilize funds even from the outsiders if the members fail to respondent readily so that the nearby premises at Centre Point might not be lost and in materializing such an objective, all concerned in the respondent-company acted bona fide only its interest as such, this misconceived petition is liable to be Amin, in one hand did everything and took all dismissed. 

38. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate, appeared on behalf of the respondent nos. 3,4 and 16 He submitted that all the respondent Nos. 2 to 16 strangers to the respondent-company, acted bona fide and in good-faith, in purchasing its shares for value, the receipts for which were duly granted by respondent no. 17 the Chairman, Dr. Ruhul Amin, the Managing Director and Dr. Gafoor, the Financial Director of the respondent-company. He submitted further that the respondent nos. 2 to 16 were invited by no other person than by Dr. Ruhul Amin the Managing Director himself, to the attend the meeting of the Board of Directors on 17th May, 2002, as observers and in compliance to his request they duly attended the said meeting only as observers but did not participate in the deliberations of the  meeting, as such, the allegations of threat or application of force, raised against them, was absolutely false, besides, on their appointment as directors they were all felicitated by Dr. Ruhul Amin himself, in the meeting of the Board of Directors held on 20th June, 2002, The learned Advocate further submitted that all the papers made available show that the decision to issue further. share were taken unanimously by the Board of Directors which was also duly endorsed by the company in its 14yh Annual General Meeting, that the notices to the existing share-holders were directed to be issued and some of them duly responded, that all these facts on record, raised a reasonable presumption that all the procedures required under the articles, were duly complied with and they had no way of knowing that the Managing Director did not take necessary steps to issue the required notice to the petitioner who is no less than a person that the brother of his wife. The learned Advocate highlighted in his submissions that Dr. Ruhul respondent-company starting from allotment of shares in favour of the respondents nos. 2 to 16 received the value of the shares from them, ensuring their presence in both the meeting of the Board of Directors on 17th May and 20th June, 2002, even he himself felicited them on behalf of the respondent-company on their appointment as its directors but on the other hand, he himself challenged all his own actions and steps taken on behalf of the 'respondent-company in respect of allotment of is shares in favour of the respondent nos. 2 to 16 by swearing an affidavit on 3rd April, 2003, purported to be on behalf of the respondent-company and in its interest but as matter of fact, in full and naked support of the instant petition, which apparently supplemented it. The learned Advocate submitted further that Dr. Ruhul Amin in order to maintain his control over the respondent-company and also to suppress and hide his own illegal activities, arranged to file the instant petition, using the name of his brother-in-law, through an attorney who is admittedly his own relation and an employee, unnecessarily showing himself as representing the respondent company but -without impleading him, in order to create an opportunity for him to file an affidavit-in-opposition purportedly on behalf of the respondent-company but fully and wholly supplementing the petition itself in complete derogation to the interest of the respondent-company but only to serve his own interest. The learned Advocate pointed out that when Dr. Ruhul Amin could lend one of his own employees to file the petition on behalf of the petitioner and also filed a voluminous affidavit-in-opposition, in support of the petition, instead of justifying the actions of the respondent-company and when he is so much helpful to the petitioner, it is hardly believable that he did not inform his brother-in-law, the petitioner, about the further issue of shares, The learned Advocate finally submitted that in the instant petition, Dr. Ruhul Amin is the real petitioner who engineered the filing of this petition in the name of his brother-in-law, which was signed and filed by one of his employees. 

39. In reply to all these submissions, Dr, Zahir furiously retorted that it does not matter how the Managing Director behaved in running the respondent-company but if there is a breach in the pre-emptory right given under Article 7 of the Articles of Association, the petitioner has a right to participate in the further issue of shares in proportion to the shares held by him. 

40. In answer to the question as to why the Managing Director of the respondent company did not ensure issuance of notices offering the shares to its members, as resolved by Board of Directors in his presence, Dr. Zahir replied that that is not his job. When asked what is his job as the Managing Director he could not respond, When asked as to how the notices were issued when further shares were earlier issued, the learned Advocate was unable to explain. 
In this regard, Dr. Shahid Udding Ahmed, the respondent no 17 deposed as follows in his examination in chief: 
"Q. Who had the responsibility of circulating the memo dated 09.10.2001 amongst the existing share-holders? 
A. Obviously it is the Managing Director Dr. Ruhul Amin who was maintaining the office of the company. He was not cross-examined on this statement but stated in reply to other questions as follows. 
Q. Do you have any prove that Dr. Monjurul Islam was served with the notice or he refused in writing to participate in disputed allotment and transfers? 
A. I have no proof. 
Q. In this particular case who issued notice of allotment issued to the existing share holders?
 A. It is the Managing Director. 
Q. Is it correct that despite the duty of M. D. you have taken the duty to serve Annexure-14 to the share holder?
 A. It is not correct, 1 did not serve annexure-14, this is the job of Managing Director. 
From the papers and documents filed on behalf of all the contesting parties and also from the depositions it is apparent the further issue of shares were made in the interest of the respondent-company alone and not for any collateral purpose. 

41. I have already held that inspite of discretion of the Board of Directors to offer the further shares to any person the guide line in such matters, as provided in Article 7 in the Articles of Association, has to be followed, As regards offer of further share to the petitioner, the contention made on behalf of the petitioner at paragraph-6 to the petition as well as in the deposition of his attorney is that no such offer was made to the petitioner before those were allotted in favour of the respondent nos. 2 to 16. It was also stated in paragraph-7 of the petition that the petitioner was not even offered the shares transferred by the respondent nos. 18 and 19. 
The petitioner lives at Chittagong while his attorney at Dhaka. The attorney gave the following declarations in his affidavit attached to the petition on 23rd July 2002 as follows:
 "1. That I am constituted Attorney and Tadbirkar of the case on behalf of the petitioner and as such I am acquainted with the facts and Circumstances of the case and I am competent and authorized to swear this affidavit on behalf of the petitioner of the petition. 
2. That the statements made above are true to my knowledge and belief." 
In reply an affidavit-in-opposition was sworn by Dr. Md. Shaheeduddin Ahmed, the respondent no. 17. It was contended a paragraph 9 (h) to the affidavit-in-opposition that in pursuant to the decisions of the Board of Directors taken on 6th October, 2001 a memo dated 9th October, 2001, offering the further issue of shares, was circulated to all the share-holders under the signatures of both the respondents no. 17 and Dr. Ruhul Amin. It was contended at paragraph 9(i) that seven share-holders made partial payment in response to the offer of shares. 
In the face of these conflicting facts, the attorney of the petitioner stated as follows.
 Q. How do you know that Dr. Monjurul Islam received no notice dated 09.10.2001 as annexed in Annexure-14 to the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondents nos. 1 and 17?
A.  He has told me so.
Q. I am suggesting to you that since you neither live in Chittagong nor are you authorized by the petitioner to receive notices on his behalf regarding the affairs of the company, you do not have any personal knowledge in this matter.
 A. Yes, I have no personal knowledge. 
This petition under Section 43 praying for rectification of the share-register of the company on he ground that he was not offered the relevant shares before allotted to the outsiders but no efforts were made to prove the said allegation excepting only by a vague statement of the attorney. 

42. It is not the case of the petitioner that since allotment of one hundred shares in his favour he always participated in the further issue of shares made earlier from time to time or that this time he was purposely left out. No enmity was alleged by the petitioner against the respondent no 17 of any of the directors, rather, Dr. Ruhul Amin, the Managing Director, his brother-in-law, supported the petitioner all the way even at the cost of the respondent-company. It appears that the petitioner could not even mention in his petitions the date of allotment of the shares in his favour. Besides, there is no record of his further participation in the next issue of shares of the respondent-company. 

43. Under such circumstances a mere vague hearsay statement of the attorney is not enough and convincing to establish the case of the petitioner that he did not receive the notice dated 9th October, 2001 offering him the proportionate number of shares as alleged on behalf of the respondent no. 17. 

44. In order to appreciate and understand the petition and the contentions let me refer to the facts, on record a bit further. 

45. It appears that the petitioner is the brother-in-law of Dr. Ruhul Amin. He neither deposed nor sworn an affidavit in support of the petition. The instant petition was filed by one Mr. Harisul Haque on behalf of the petitioner. He swore affidavit and also deposed as his attorney. The said attorney is an employee of Dr. Ruhul Amin and is also his relation. In his deposition he stated as follows. 
Q. What is your occupation?
A.  Pharmacist. 
Q. In which pharmacy do you work?
A. Al-Raji Hospital Pharmacy. 
Q. Are you related to Dr. Ruhul Amin?
A. Yes, I am related to Dr. Ruhul Amin." 
Q. Is the resolution dated 25.01.2003 submitted in Court by respondent no. 17 as Annexure-1 to his affidavit is a genuine one" 
A. No
Q. Was any meeting of Baord of directors held on 25.01.2002 ?
A. No. 
Q. Who is the Chairman of the Company? 
A. Previously it used to be Dr. Shahiduddin not (now) it is Dr. Abdur Rahman.
Q. When did Dr. Abedur Rahman became Chairman of the Company? 
A. I do not recollect the exact date probably last year October or November.
Q. Are you a Director or share holder of the company in your personal capacity?
A. No. 
Q. Is the petitioner a Director of the company?
A. No. 
Q. Does the petitioner attend Board Meetings of the Company? 
A. No.
Q. Does the petitioner ordinarily receive copies of minutes of the Board Meetings of the Company or extracts thereof?
 A. No, he does not and he is not supposed to receive copies of minutes or extracts thereof. 
Q. On what basis have you testified that ennexures-12 and 83 of the affidavit in opposition, which are minutes of Board Meeting are fabricated documents? 
A. I have stated that this documents are fabricated by comparing Annexure-12 and Annexure-14. Annexure-83 is fabricated because it was originally a hand written document and the document annexed as Annexure-83 to the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent nos. 1 and 17 is typed. The original hand written one is with the legal advisor. 
Q. Who is the legal adviser? 
A. A. K. M. Badruddoza. 
Q. Have our seen only this document with the lawyer of the company or other documents are lying with him?
 A. There are other documents lying with the lawyer of the company. 
Q. Were you present at the meeting of the Board of Directors dated 17,05.2002?
A. No. 
Q. Was Dr. Mnjurul Islam personally present in the meeting dated 17.05.2002?
 A. No. 
Q. Are you personally authorized to receive notices on behalf of the petitioner relating to the affairs of the company?
 A. No. Q. 
Q. How do you know that Dr. Monjurul Islam received no notice dated 09.10.200D as annexed in Annexure-14 to the affidavit in opposition of the respondents nos. 1 and 17?
 A. He has told me so.
Q. Do you have any idea of how much money was receive from the new share holder and ho this money was spent? 
A. I have no personal knowledge I have heard that these monies have been deposited in the account of the company. 
Q. I am suggesting to you that since you neither live in Chittagong nor are you authorized by the petitioner to receive notices on his behalf regarding the affairs of the company you do not have any personal knowledge in this matter.
A. Yes, I have no personal knowledge.

46. From the scrutiny of the above noted depositions of Md. Harisul Haque, it appears that by profession he is pharmacist. Neither the petitioner nor he is a member of the Board of Directors of the respondent-company. They do not attend the meetings of the Board. Neither the petitioner receive any copy of the minutes of the meeting of the Board of Directors nor his attorney is personally authorized to receive notices on his behalf relating to the affairs of the company. Besides the petitioner lives at Chittagong while his attorney lives in Dhaka.

47. It appears that the attorney happens to know the ins and outs of the respondent-company. He knows who was the previous Chairman and who is present one. He knows when the meetings of the Board of Directors were held and when it was .not. He can say what resolutions of the meeting is genuine and which one is not. He can- easily detect by a mere comparison-and state on oath as to which resolutions are fabricated and which ones are genuine. He also knows the whereabouts of he original documents.

 48. It appears that this attorney, although a .mere pharmacist, knows more about the company than possible its Managing Director. Still he says, 'I have no personal knowledge. Then who has? Certainly not the petitioner. He leads an innocent life at Chittagong far from the maddening crowd of Dhaka, leaving all responsibility to his attorney. That leaves one person, Dr. Ruhul Amin, the Managing Director of the respondent-company and a near relation of the petitioner. Let me examine his role in this matter. 

49. In this petition, Dr. Ruhul Amin was not made a party either in his personal capacity or in the capacity of the Managing Director of the company but without making him a party, as such he was shown to represent the respondent-company in the cause-title of the petition. But why and how he was made to so represent the company was not stated in the body of the petition itself. No paper has been filed authorizing him by the Board of Directors to represent the respondent-company. He however filed an okalatnama, executed by himself as the Managing Director of the respondent-company and entered appearance on its behalf on 14th December 2002. In due course, he filed an affidavit in opposition on 3rd April 2003. 

50. At the time of filing of the petition under Section 43 of the Companies Act, an application praying for an order of injunction restraining the respondent nos. 2 to 16 from attending any meeting of the respondent-company was also filed. Another identical 
application, supporting the allegations of the petitioner in his petition for injunction, was sworn and filed by Dr. Ruhul Amin on 14th December, 2002, Praying for an order of injunction restraining the respondent nos. 2 to 16 from holding the annual general meeting, as notified in a notice dated 4th December, 2002, or any other meeting of the respondent-company till disposal of the petitioner's application for rectification of share register.
After hearing, this Court by its order dated 18.12.2003, rejected both the petitions for injunction.
 In the said petition for injunction.Dr. Ruhul Amin, however, did not raise any allegations of fraud, forgery or fabrication, in allotting the shares in favour of the respondent nos. 2 to 16. In the affidavit-in-opposition sworn by Dr. Ruhul Amin on 3rd April, 2002, annexed the minutes of the proceedings of a meeting of the Board of Directors allegedly held. on 13th July, 2002 (Annexure-L) The minutes of the said meeting was signed by Dr. Ruhul Amin and the earliest document on record showing his alleged disapproval of the decisions taken on 17th May, 2002. But even on that date, no allegations of fraud, forgery or fabrication of the minutes of the meetings held on different dates, by the Board of Directors was not raised or mentioned. As such a serious doubt is raised about such belated allegations stated in the affidavit-in-opposition sworn on 3rd April 2003. 

51.The Annexure-L, annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by Dr. Ruhul Amin, however, shows that even before filing of the instant petition for rectification, the resolutions of the Board of Directors taken of 17the May, 2002, were allegedly stayed and the respondents no. 17 was removed in the meeting of the Board of Directors, allegedly held on, 13th July, 2002, replaced by Dr. Abdur Rahman as the Chairman of the respondent-company but no mention of the said meeting was stated in the petition for injunction sworn by Dr. Ruhul Amin of .14th December, 2002, as such the genuineness of Annexure-L, is now in question. Besides, the minutes of the annual general meeting alleged to be held on 8th December, 2002 (Annexure-2 to the petition for injunction), does not show that the respondents no. 17 had already been removed earlier as the Chairman. 

52. The papers annexed to the petition for injunction and the affidavit-in-opposition, both sworn by Dr. Ruhul Amin show that he wanted to remove the respondent no. 17 as the Chairman of the company and also wanted to undo the allotment of shares in favour of the respondents nos. 2 to 16, made in he meeting of the Board of Directors held on 17th May, 2002 and confirmed in the meeting held on .20th June, 2002. 

53. The above mentioned petition for injunction and in the affidavit-in-opposition filed on 3rd April, 2003, Dr. Ruhul Amin not only supported the allegations of the petitioner and supplemented it in all possible ways but also took much more initiative in the matter than the passive petitioner. 
It should be noted in this connection that Dr. Ruhul Amin is unable to maintain a petition under Section 43 by invoking Article 7 of the .articles of association, because he himself was a party in making allotment of shares in favour of the respondent nos. 2 to 16

54. It may be mentioned that prior to the filing of this petition for rectification, another suit being Title Suit. no. 127 of 2002 was filed on 8th July, 2002, in the Court of Joint District Judge, Fourth Court Dhaka, by Mr. Toufiqul Islam, brother of the petitioner and another, as appearing from the affidavits-in-opposition filed on behalf of the respondents nos. 17, 3 and 4 praying for declaration, inter alia, that the allotment shares in the meeting of the Boars of Directors held on 17th May, 2002, and appointment of directors and the proceedings of the subsequent meeting held on 20th June were illegal without jurisdiction etc. and also sought temporary injunction against implementation of the resolutions dated 17th May, 2002 and having failed to achieve their objectives, the present petition has been initiated. 

55. On the basis of these facts and circumstances, allegations are raised on behalf of the respondents nos. 4 and 17 that it is Dr. Rubul Amin, the Managing Director of the respondent-company by using the name of the petitioner, the brother of his wife, filed the instant petition for rectification, through his own employee and relation Md. Harisul Haque, These allegations cannot be ruled out. 

56. Since the identity of the actual petitioner is in serious doubt and since the allegations of fraud forgery and fabrication in respect of the different resolutions and decisions of the Board of Directors of the respondent-company have been raised., involving complicated questions of disputed facts of serious nature, requiring further examination of evidence in details which is not possible in this forum, the instant petition is liable to be dismissed. In that view of the matter., this petition for rectification is dismissed but without any order as to cost. 

57. Before parting with this matter, I would like to observe that because of anomaly between sub-section, 1 and sub section 2 of Section 155 of the companies Act, 1994, the real spirit behind the said provision is being frustrated. Instead of bringing improvements, the amendment of Section 105C of the Companies Act, 1913 to its present position, has rather created confusion. 

58.As such, I would like to recommend that the amendment as proposed in the Report of the Company Law Reforms Committee of 1981, should be accepted in this regard in its entirety which is as follows: 
"155 (1) where the directors decide to increase the subscribed capital of the company by issue of further shares within the limit of authorized capital then — 
(a) Such further shares shall be offered to the members in proportion, as nearly as circumstances admit, to the capital paid up on the existing share held by such member (irrespective of class) at the date of the offer. 
(b) Such offer shall be made by notice specifying the number of shares offered and limiting a time not being less than 15 days from the date of the offer within which the offer, if not accepted, will be deemed to have been declined. 
(c) Unless the articles of the company otherwise provide, the offer aforesaid shall be deemed to include a right exercisable by the person concerned to renounce the share offered to him or any of them  in favour of any other person whether a member or not; and the notice referred to in clause (b) shall contain a statement of this right; 
(d) At the expiry of the time specified in the notice aforesaid or on receipt of earlier instruction from the members to whom such notice is given that the declines to accept the shares offered the directors may dispose of the same in such manner as they may think most beneficial to the company, the directors may likewise dispose of any such further shares (by reason of the ratio which such shares bear to capital paid up on share held by members entitled to an offer of such shares) cannot, in the opinion of the directors be offered under this section.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) the further shares aforesaid may be offered to any person whether or not those persons include the person referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (1) by the company in general meeting in any manner whatsoever, provided that when such further shares or any part of it are offered to the existing members of the company the same shall be in proportion to the capital paid up on the existing shares held by each such member irrespective of class. 
(3) Nothing in this section shall be deemed to authorize the directors or the company in general meeting as the case may be—
(a) to enlarge the time within which the offer should be accepted, or, 
(b) to authorize any member to exercise the right of renunciation for a second time on he ground that a person in whose favour the renunciation was first made had declined to take the shares comprised in he renunciation.
(4) In the case of a private company the right of renunciation as contained in clause (c) of sub-section (1) shall be available only in favour of an existing member. (5) Nothing in sub-section (2) shall apply to a private company."
 59. Let a copy of this judgment be forwarded to the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Government of Bangladesh, for doing the needful in this regard. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Muhammad Dastagir Hussain J: Let the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner do from part of the main application. 

2. In an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh the petitioner has sought for direction upon the government to investigate the connection of sonic judicial officer with a banned religious organization namely “জামাতুল মুজাহিদীন বাংলাদেশ।”

3. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner is celebrated journalist and a peace activist and as per Article 21 of Constitution the petitioner has public duty to protect the legal system of the country. The learned Advocate submits- that a report was published on 28th September. 2006 in a daily newspaper wherein it has been stated that নিম্ন আদালতের বেশ কিছু বিচারকদের সঙ্গে নিষদ্ধ ঘোষিত ইসলামী জঙ্গী সংগঠন জামাতুল মুজাহিদীন বাংলাদেশের (জেএমবি) ঘনিষ্ঠ যোগাযোগ আছে বলে অভিযোগ পাওয়া গেছে, Also he submits that in another writ petition filed before this Court the petitioner of that writ petition has also entangled the respondent No.3 with the said organization and as such to protect the Constitution as well as legal system of the country the matter is required to be investigated by the proper authority as Per law. The petitioner prays for a direction from this' Court regarding investigation into the matter. It has been further submitted that the public functionaries are under legal obligation to act in accordance with law. The learned Advocate -appearing on behalf of. The Petitioner relied upon the decision referred 4 in 10 BLT (AD) 108. 

4. Heard the learned Advocate perused the application and Annexures. It appears that the instant application has been filed by the petitioner on the basis of a report published in a daily newspaper in connection with certain criminal eases. On perusal on the same it appears that the petitioner has no locustandi in the instant case as he is not affected in any manner and the facts of the case as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner has not applicable in the instant case. Furthermore certain vague and fictitious matters were raised in this application .which cannot be examined by this court by way of judicial view exercising the power confirmed under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh: The contentions as raised by the petitioner. against the Senior judicial officers of the Republic arc baseless and also there arc alternative provisions available for determination of such issues. 

5. On perusal of the application we do not find any violation of the fundamental rights of the petitioner as guaranteed in Chapter-III of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh or any violation of law. The application itself is frivolous one and brought with an intention to affect the integrity and efficiency of the judicial of the country. 

6. Under these facts and circumstances we find no. reasons to interfere. Hence the application is rejected in limine. 
End.

lawyer:
Mr. Kazi Md. Tanvir Islam, Advocate ------ For the petitioner. 
Mr. A.Q.M. Safiullah, with Mr. Ruhul Amen, with Rokeya Akhter and Mr. Tanveer Awal, Advocate ------ For the respondent No. 2.
parties:
Mrs. Delwara Begum
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Bangladesh, Secretariat, Ramna, Dhaka and others
full_judgment:
A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J: On an application at the instance of the petitioner a Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why discriminatory treatment to the petitioner and inaction of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot in the Purbachal New wn project as affected person in compliance with the provision of Article 8 (ka) of প্লট  বরাদ্দ নীতিমালা Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha as well as of the decision taken in the Board Meeting of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakha dated 23.09.2010 and 26.09.2010 (Annexure-F) should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents should not be directed to give allotment of a plot of 5 (five) katha in favour of the petitioner in the "Purbachal New Town" project as affected person vide award serial Numbers: 45 (Dha). 55 (Ja), 59 (Cha) and security deposit slip No. 26805 and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Relevant facts necessary for disposal of the instant rule is that the petitioner is a peace loving and law abiding permanent citizen of Bangladesh. She is now residing of the address given in the cause title.

3. The respondent No. 1 is the Government of Bangladesh represented by its Secretary Ministry of Housing and Public Works who is responsible for farming of Government policy. Respondent No. 2 is the highest officer of the Rajdhani Unnayon Kartipakkha. Respondent No. 3-6 are responsible functionaries under respondent No. 2 and all of them are responsible for implementation of Government policy.

4. The petitioner purchased 16.5 decimals of land from one Hasen Ali vide registered deed No. 2080 dated 22.02.1995 situated at C.S. khatian No. 300, 310, S.A. khatian No. 347, 330, 360, C.S and S.A. Plot No. 30, R.S. khatian No. 84, R.S. Plot No. 46, 59, 63, Mouza-Poshi, Police Station Rupgonj, District-Narayangonj.

5. The petitioner got possession of the said land and got her name mutated under mutation case No. 2409 of 1994-1995 and paid rents to the Government in respect of her total land measuring 16.5 decimals.

6. While the petitioner was peacefully owning and possessing the said land, the Government decided to acquire the said land along with some other lands for the requiring body namely Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha and ultimately the land was acquired under L.A Case No. 20 of 1993-1994 and at the time of acquisition the Government published a notification in the daily newspaper that in future the sufferers of the acquisition would be allotted plots in the new project.

7. The petitioner applied for compensation award against her acquired land by submitted all relevant title deeds and papers and the office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (L.A) having been satisfied as to the ownership of the petitioner gave compensation money with award.

8. The Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha subsequently published advertisement inviting applications from the interested persons for allotment of plots under different projects namely. "Extended Uttara Residential Area (third phase) project, Purbachal New City project and the petitioner being affected person in response to the said advertisement, filed application for getting a plot measuring 5 kathas by deposition required amount of 'II. 50,000/- (fifty Thousand) for the Purbachal New City project hereinafter referred as to the project.

9. The person whose land is acquired is entitled to get priority of allotment of the plot if the acquisition is for the residential purpose and in this regard a gazette was published on 15th January, 1970 as Dhaka gazette wherein it was provided that "Subject to the provision of clause B of sub-section 101 of the act valid application of the person who had either land or residential house in the area acquired for the development of Township, shall have the first preference for allotment, provided that he/She applied for allotment and fulfilled other conditions. RAJUK set up a nitimala for allotment of plot of the affected person as 8 (ka) and 8 (kha) and the petitioner is within the nitimala of 8 (ka). The petitioners land is acquired and she has fulfilled all the required conditions and made application in proper form.

10. The Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha already started giving allotment and also allotted many plots to their chosen persons and though already more than 15 years have elapsed from the date of filing application with requisite amount of Tk. 50,000/- (Fifty Thousand), the petitioner did not receive any response or information from the authority as to her allotment of the plot as she is entitled to get preference in allotment of plot under the project.

11. The petitioner owned land measuring 16.5 decimals for residential purpose and except the said acquired land she has no other piece of land within Dhaka city and due to such acquisition she became landless in this city.

12. It is evident from the minutes of the Board meeting of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha dated 23.09.2010 and 26.09.2010 that there is clear admission by RAJUK that the people whose 0.1650 acre of land or more than that have been acquired are entitled to have a plot and accordingly, the said board meeting recommended allotment of plots in favour of 700 affected persons.

13. The Rajuk gave allotment of plot in favour of more than 700 affected persons at Narayangonj side and 804 persons at Gazipur side of the project as per Nitimala enunciated in 8 (ka) and 8 (kha) and the list of allottee of affected category has duly been published in the official website of RAJUK.

14. It is stated that place in such a situation the petitioner through her learned lawyer served a Notice Demanding Justice to the respondents for allotment of a plot in her favour, but no response has yet been received till today.

15. Mr. Kazi Md. Tanvir Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. A.Q.M. Safiullah, with Mr. Ruhul Amin, Ms. Rokeya Akhter and Mr. Tanveer Awal, Advocates for the respondents.

16. Mr. Kazi Md. Tanvir Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the provision regarding allotment of the plots is that the affected persons shall have first preference for getting allotment but the respondents without considering the legitimate right of the petitioner already allotted many plots to their chosen persons and not taking any steps for giving allotment in favour of the petitioner and as such the discriminatory treatment of a plot in the project is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

17. The learned Advocate next submits that since 700 affected persons have been selected for allotment on the criterion that they are awardees of 0.1650 acre of land, the petitioner being equally affected standing on the same footing is entitled to have allot but the respondents with malafide motive discriminating the petitioner with them depriving her legitimate right and as such the discriminatory treatment and inaction of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot to the petitioner in the project is liable to be declared as illegal and without lawful authority and the respondents should be directed to give allotment of a plot of 5 katha in favour of the petitioner from the project.

18. The learned Advocate further submits that since the petitioner is an awardee of .1650 acre of land, she is entitled to have a plot under Article 8 of the RAJUK as well as the decision and recommendation taken in the Board meeting of RAJUK dated 23.09.2010 and 26.09.2010 and more over 700 affected persons having selected for allotment on the criterion as above and as such the discriminatory treatment and inaction of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot in the project is illegal and the respondents should be directed to give allotment of a plot to the petitioner from the project within 6 (six) months.

19. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the inaction of the respondents to comply with the Article 8 (Ka) of the প্লট  বরাদ্দ  নীতিমালা  of RAJUK as well as its decision equally in respect of the petitioner like as the 700 others who have been selected for allotment of plot is discriminatory, arbitrary, malafide and a clear violation of fundamental rights of the petitioner guaranteed under Article 27 and 31 of the Constitution.

20. The learned advocate in support of his contention has referred two unreported decision passed in writ petition No. 1781 of 2011 and in writ petition No. 7628 of 2012 in which one of us was a party.

21. Mr. A.Q.M. Shafiullah, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the respondent No. 2 contested the rule by filing affidavit in opposition to controvert the statements as made in the writ petition but verbally opposed the rule.

22. Mr. A.Q.M. Shafiullah, the learned Advocate liar the respondent No. 2 submits that the writ petition (hereinafter referred to as the petition) have been served upon the respondent No. 2. I have gone through the said petition and understood the contents thereof. I have been advised to controvert only those statements which are relevant for disposal of the above petition and the statements which are not specifically admitted herein shall be deemed to have been denied by this deponent.

23. He next submits that the statements made in paragraph Nos. 4 and 5 of the petition to the effect that the petitioners were the owners of 16.5 decimals of land of Mouza Porshi, Police Station Rupgonj, District-Narayangonj and in respect of the same her name was mutated under mutation case No. 2409 /1994-1995 and paid rents to the Government regularly being matters of record need to reply.

24. He lastly submits that the statements made in paragraphs Nos. 6 and 7 of the petition it is stated that the Government decided to acquire some lands for the requiring body namely Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakhaya (RAJUK) and ultimately Government acquired in total 5,500 acres of land including 16.5 decimals of land of the petitioner in two projects having 4000 acres at Narayangonj District and other 1500 acres from Gazipur District Under different projects namely extended Uttara Residential Area 3rd Phase Project and Purbachal new City Project. The petitioner was given compensation of the land in question. After acquisition of the total land the Deputy Commissioner of Narayangonj and Gazipur Districts handed over the said acquired land to Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkhaya (RAJUK) for implementation of the projects in allotting the plots of different persons.

25. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner, perused the writ petition and the annexures filed thereto and considered the materials on record. It appears from Annexure 'F' to the writ petition that is minutes of the 911' Board meeting of Rajuk dated 23.09.2010 and 26.09.2010 that the concerned Ministry had recommended for allotment of plots in favour of the awardees of 0.1650 acres of land as affected persons. The Board of Rajuk also decided to allot plots to 560 persons on the criterion that 0.1650 acres of land had been acquired from each of them and as such they were entitled to a plot under Article 8 (ka) of the of Rajuk. However, it appears from the same minutes that the fate of 54 persons including the petitioner whose award had been subsequently added on her application to make her eligible for allotment on the same criterion remained pending.

<u>26. Since 560 persons have been selected for allotment of plots on consideration that they are awardees 01 0.1650 acres of land, we do not see any valid reason for excluding the petitioner from such benefit, since they are equally affected, although by subsequent addition of their awards we do not find any legal reason for denied of her such entitlement whom people standing on the same footing were selected for such allotment, since main criterion as set by Rajuk is awardee of 0.1650 acres of land and names of 560 selected persons have been published in the daily newspaper on such consideration we are of the view that the petitioner is also jointly entitled to have on 5 (five) katha plot allotted in her favour of lands are available with Rajuk for such allotment.</u>

27. We find support of this view in a decision of our Apex Court. We find the provision regarding allotment of the plots the affected persons shall have first preference for getting allotment but the respondents without considering the legitimate right of the petitioner already allotted many plots to their chosen persons and not taking any steps for giving allotment in favour of the petitioner which amounts to discriminatory treatment of a plot in the project and such attitude of the authority is very much arbitrary, malafide and the same is hereby declared as act done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

28. We further find since 700 affected persons have been selected for allotment on the criterion that they are awardees of 0.1650 acre of lands the petitioner being equally affected standing on the same footing is entitled to have a plot but the respondents with malafide motive discriminating the petitioner with them depriving her legitimate right and as such the discriminatory treatment and inaction of the respondents in giving allotment of a plot to the petitioner is hereby declared as illegal and without lawful authority and the respondents are hereby directed to give allotment of a plot of 5 katha in favour of the petitioner from the project.

29. We also find that the inaction of the respondents to comply with the Article 8 (ka) of the of Rajuk as well as its decision equally in respect of the petitioner like as the 700 others who have been selected for allotment of plot is discriminatory arbitrary, malafide and a clear violation of fundamental rights of the petitioner as guaranteed under Article 27 and 31 of the Constitution held in Rajuk-Vs. Jahanara Begum and others reported in 12 BLT (AD) (2004) page 222 wherein modifying the order passed by the High Court Division, the Appellate Division directed the Rajuk to scrutiny the petition filed by the writ petitioner for allotment of plot and to allot plots in their favour if they satisfied the condition and criteria set down by the Rajuk entitled a person to have allotment of plot as affected person provided Rajuk has available lands for such allotment.

30. We find merit in the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner. Accordingly, the rule is made absolute. There will be no order as to cost.

31. In relying the said decision of our Apex Court, we hold that since the petitioner has prima facie fulfilled the criterion in the instant case namely she is awardee of 0.1650 acres of land like other 560 selected allottees she is also entitled to have a 5 (five) katha plot allotted in her favour as applied for provided Rajuk has available land for such allotment in favour of the petitioner in the purbachal New Town project as affected person vide award serial numbers 45 (Dha), 55 (Ja), 59 (Cha) and security deposit slip No. 26805; and the respondents are hereby directed to give allotment of a plot measuring 5 (five) kathas in the Purbachal New Town Project in favour of the petitioner as affected person within three months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment positively.

32. The office is hereby directed to transmit a copy of this Judgment to the concern authority forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Khaleda Panna, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Mr. A. S. M. Nazmul Hoque, D.A.G with Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam, A.A.G. ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Rahima Begum
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh and Others
full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan, J: In this petition, filed under Article 102 of the Constitution, a Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo No. ৬সি/৭৯-৭/০৬৯৩১/৭ dated 17.02.2014 passed by respondent No. 4 directing to stop the MPO of the petitioner being Index No. 1032015 under Shakhipur Islamia High School (3601071301), Upazilla Vhedaergonj, District-Shariatpur (Annexure-H) shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for the disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that the petitioner applied for the post of assistant teacher on 19.01.2005, pursuant to a newspaper advertisement dated 11.01.2005. She having been found qualified, a letter dated 28.02.2005, signed by the Headmaster of the said school, was sent to the petitioner and she has joined in the said school on 01.03.2005, as Assistant Teacher. Thereafter, on 02.04.2009, by a Memo under reference জেঃশিঃঅঃ(শঃ)/১৬১ dated 02.04.2009 (Annexure-E) the Director General of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Audidaptor, Dhaka, has upgraded her salary scale from 4100 taka to 5100 taka. The petitioner was allowed MPO facilities. She has been drawing the government portion of her salary under the MPO scheme since 2006 to January 2014, vide the annexure as Annexure-F series. Further case of the petitioner is that, in view of a circular No. সংখ্যা-শিম/শাঃ১১/৭-১/২০০৯/৩৮৪ dated 18.05.2010 (Annexure-G) issued by the Ministry of Education under signature of the Secretary of the Ministry, she is absolutely qualified from the post she has been appointed. But, all on a sudden, by a Memo No. ৬সি/৭৯-ম/০৬/৯৩১/৭ dated 17.02.2014 (Annexure-H), the MPO facilities i.e. the government portion of the salary of the petitioner has been temporarily stopped. In this background and challenging the legality of aforesaid letter dated 17.02.2014 (Annexure-H), this writ petition has filed, moved as a motion and the present rule has been issued.

3. The respondent No. 2 has appeared and filed an affidavit in opposition denying all materials allegation and further stating that based on an inquiry it was found that the petitioner has submitted academic certificates in which she has shown that she obtained 2nd Division, vide the Provisional Certificate of B.A (pass) Examination 1995. The inquiry was held by the District Education Officer and he has directed the petitioner to submit the certificates before him for his verification. But, as reflected in a inquiry report, sent by the District Education Officer (respondent No. 6) to the Director General of Higher Secondary Education Dhaka (respondent No. 2), under Memo No. জেঃশিঃঅঃ/শঃ/৯১৭(৫)dated 17.02.2010, it has been stated amongst other, that the petitioner by resorting to forgery had shown 2nd Division in her HSC and B.A (Pass) Certificate and that the Headmaster and Members of the Managing Committee were requested to submits the educational certificate of the petitioner, but they did not. In that inquiry report, a recommendation was made to stop the MPO facilities of the petitioner (that inquiry report has been annexed to the affidavit in opposition as Annexure-2). The further case is of the respondent is that, the MPO facilities of the petitioner was rightly stopped and this rule has no merit.

4. The petitioner has submitted said an affidavit in reply, mainly reiterating her case as stated in the writ petition and further asserting that the investigation committee never allowed the petitioner to participate in purported proceeding and deliberation of the said team. The petitioner was neither given any opportunity to controvert the allegations or the records relied upon by the respondents, nor the petitioner was supplied with any materials concerning the said proceeding. Hence this inquiry report is not sustainable; nor relevant for investigation. This rather amounts to clear violation of the principal of the natural justice.

5. The learned advocate Mr. Khaleda Panna, being instructed by learned advocate Mr. Mohammad Mujibur Rahman, appeared for the petitioner. She has taken as through the writ petition and other materials on record. Referring to the averments made in the writ petition and to the documents annexed therewith, the learned advocate for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was appointed and she has joined on 01.03.2005, as Assistant Teacher, in Shakhipur Islamia High School, pursuant to the appointment letter dated 28.02.2005. The Director General (DG), Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, Dhaka, has upgraded her salary scale from Taka 4100 to 5100 in recognition of her passing B. Ed examination. The petitioner, she proceeds, has been drawing the government portion of her salary under the MPO scheme since 2006 to January 2014 as will be evident from Annexure-F series. But, all on a sudden, by the impugned letter, issued under reference শিম/শাঃ১৩/পরিদর্শন-৭/২০০৯/০৮ dated 15.01.2014, the MPO of the petitioner has been temporarily suspended and that has not been restored till today. As such, the suspension of MPO is illegal for not following the concerned regulations in the matter of suspension of MPO as well as the impugned order of suspension is not temporary is effect. Besides, the impugned memo has been issued in clear violation principal of natural justice, arbitrary and is malafide. She next submits that, as per circular No. শিম/শাঃ১১/৭-১/২০০৯/৩৮৪ dated 18.05.2010 (Annexure-G) issued under signature of the Secretary of the Ministry, the petitioner is competent to be appointed and to continue her services as the assistant teacher of the said school. By this circular, she adds, all persons holding 3rd Divisions have been declared competent for such appointment and continuation of their service. Therefore, under no circumstances the MPO of the petitioner can be suspended and the impugned memo has been issued without complying with the principal of natural justice or the applicable regulation and the same is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, she further submits. Accordingly she has prayed for making the rule absolute.

6. The Learned Deputy Attorney General Mr. A. S. M. Nazmul Hoque, appearing along with the learned Assistant Attorney General Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam, on the contrary, having placed the affidavit in opposition and drawing our attention to the annexure-B to the writ petition, first up all submits that in her application dated 19.01.2005 (Annexure-B), the petitioner has stated that she obtained 3rd Divisions in B.A. (pass) examination held in 1995 under the National University. But she has submitted a certificate of B.A (pass) examination showing that she has obtained 2nd Divisions in the said examination. Besides, she has also shown 2nd Divisions in her HSC examination of 1992 held under Dhaka Board, vide the investigation report under reference জেঃশিঃঅঃ/শঃ৯১৭(৫)dated 17.02.2010, submitted by the District Education Officer (Respondent No. 6) to the Director General of Education Dhaka (Respondent No. 2). Besides, photocopies of the said two certificates have been annexed as Annexures-2C and 2B to the affidavit in opposition. Based on this investigation report, he submits, the impugned letter dated 17.02.2014, was issued temporarily stopping MPO of the petitioner. He continues that there was no illegality in issuing the said impugned letter and the rule has no merit. Hence, the same is liable to be discharged.

7. Heard the learned advocate for the both sides, perused the writ petition, affidavit in opposition filed by the respondent No. 2 and the affidavit in reply filed by the petitioner.

8. As has been stated in the writ petition, these are not disputed that the petitioner was appointed pursuant to an appointment letter dated 28.02.2005, issued under signature of the Headmaster of Shakhipur lslamia High School. She applied for the post on 19.01.2005, following an advertisement dated 11.01.2005, seeking application for the post of Assistant Teacher in the said school. The petitioner was selected and she was allowed joint on 01.03.2005 as the assistant teacher. Subsequently, the District Education Officer, by a letter dated 02.04.2009 (Annexure-E), has upgraded the scale of the petitioner (Index No. 1032015) from taka 4100 to 5100, since she has passed B. Ed examination, held in 2008. It is also not disputed that the petitioner has been drawing the government portion of her salary under the MPO scheme since 2006 till January 2014, as is evident from (Annexure-F series).

9. It is also on record that, the Ministry of Education, under the signature of the Secretary of the Ministry, has issued a circular under reference No. শিম/শাঃ১১/৭-১/২০০৯/৩৮৪ dated 18.05.2010 (annexed as Annexure-G). The contents of the said circular reads as follows:

“বেসরকারি শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান-এর প্রবিধানমালা

শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়

শাখা- ১১

সংখ্যা-শিম/শাঃ ১১/৭- ১/২০০৯/৩৮৪

তারিখঃ ০৪ জৈষ্ঠ ১8১৭

১৮ মে- ২০১০

পরিপত্র

বিযয়ঃ বেসরকারী নিম্ম মাধ্যমিক ও মাধ্যমিক বিদ্যালয়ে শিক্ষক নিয়োগ সংক্রান্ত৷

শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়ের ৪ ফেব্রুয়ারি ২০১০ তারিখের স্মারক নং- শাঃ ১৩/এমপিও- ১২/২০০৯/৭৫ মাধ্যমে

জারিকৃত "বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান (স্কুল, কলেজ, মাদ্রাসা ও কারিগরি শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানসমূহ) এর শিক্ষক ও কর্মচারীদের বেতন-ভাতাদির সরকারি অংশ প্রদান এবং জনবল কাঠামো সম্পর্কিত নির্দেশিকায়”যাই থাকুক না কেন, শিক্ষা জীবনে একাধিক তৃতীয় বিভাগ/শ্রেণী নিয়ে বেসরকারী নিম্ম মাধ্যমিক বিদ্যালয় বা বেসরকারী মাধ্যমিক বিদ্যালয়ে শিক্ষক হিসেবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত ও ইনডেক্সধারী ব্যক্তিগণ নিয়োগ সংক্রান্ত অন্যান্য শর্ত পূরণ সাপেক্ষে, যে কোন বেসরকারী নিম্ম মাধ্যমিক বিদ্যালয়ে প্রধান শিক্ষক বা সহকারী শিক্ষক এবং বেসরকারী মাধ্যমিক বিদ্যালয়ে প্রধান শিক্ষক, সহকারী প্রধান শিক্ষক বা সহকারী শিক্ষক পদে নিয়োগ লাভের যোগ্য হবেন এবং বেতন-ভাতা বাবদ সরকারি সহায়তা (এমপিও) পাবেন মর্মে শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়ের ০৩/০৮/২০০৯ তারিখের নং শিম/শাঃ ১১/৭-১/২০০৯/৮৮8 পরিপত্র বহাল থাকবে ৷

স্বাক্ষরিতঃ ১৮/৫/২০১০

(সৈয়দ আতাউর সহমান)

সচিব”

10. In the context of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we find that by the impugned Memo No. ৬সি/৭৯-৭/০৬৯৩১/৭ dated 17.02.2014 (Annexure-H) the MPO of the petitioner has been stopped since then. It has been stated in the impugned Memo that the said Memo was issued by the Assistant Director of the Directorate Education, Dhaka, to the Deputy Director, Directorate of Education, Dhaka. The content of the impugned letter reads as follows:

“উর্পযুক্ত বিষয় ও সূত্রের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে শরীয়তপুর জেলার ভেদরগঞ্জ উপজেলাধীন সখিপুর ইসলামিয়া উচ্চ বিদ্যালয় (৩৬০১০৭১৩০১)- এর সহকারী শিক্ষক জনাব রহিমা বেগম (ইনডেক্স নং- ১০৩২০১৫) এর একাধিক তৃতীয় বিভাগ নিয়ে মিথ্যা তথ্য প্রদান করে অবৈধভাবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত হওয়ায় শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়ের নির্দেশ মোতাবেক এমপিও সাময়িকভাবে স্থগিত করার প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্হা গ্রহণের জন্য তাঁকে নির্দেশক্রমে অনুরোধ করা হলো ৷

স্বাঃ

(গৌর চন্দ্র মন্ডল)

সহকারী পরিচালক (মা-২)

মাধ্যমিক ও উচ্চ শিক্ষা অধিদপ্তর

বাংলাদেশ, ঢাকা ৷”

11. As has been submitted by the learned advocate for the petitioner, we do not find any materials on record to show that before the stopping the MPO of the petitioner she was issued any notice to show cause or to explain as to why her MPO should not be stopped on the allegations leveled against her in the impugned memo, so that the petitioner could have had the opportunity to explain her position or to controvert the allegations. Besides, we do not find any inquiry committee formed to inquire into the matter of allegations brought against the petitioner in the impugned letter. Nor do we find that any notice of inquiry was served upon the petitioner to appear before an inquiry committee to place her case.

12. We have also examined the report under memo No. জেঃশিঃঅঃ/শঃ/৯১৭(৫)dated 17.02.2010, annexed as annexure-2 to the affidavit in opposition. This report was sent by the District Education Officer, Shariatpur, to the DG of the Directorate of the Education

(respondent No. 6). In this report the District Education Officer reports that an investigation was held and that he had requested the members of the Managing Committee as well as the Headmaster of the school, by sending a notice, to produce the HSC and B.A (pass) certificates of the petitioner to ascertain the fact of forgery alleged to have been committed by the petitioner (and of and another teacher/husband of the petitioner).

<u>13. As stated in this inquiry report, rather investigation report, we find that the petitioner i.e. the person aggrieved was not requested to place the disputed certificates before the Education Officer and that the investigation was held unilaterally and behind back of the petitioner. We have also examined another letter under reference শরীয়তপুর/৬সি/৭৯-ম/০৬৭৬১৬/৫ dated 19.08.2010 annexed as Annexure- 2D to the affidavit in opposition, which was sent by the Assistant Director Higher-2, the Directorate of the Education, to the Headmaster of the Shakhipur Islamia High School asking the latter to explain as to why the MPO of the petitioner and another teacher-should not be stopped for obtaining the MPO facilities by submitting forged academic certificates. We find that the allegation is brought against the petitioner (and another teacher), but this notice was served upon the Head Master, who is not to be affected for stopping the MPO and against whom no allegation was brought. The Headmaster may not be interested to produce the certificates as he has no interest in this matter. He is not the person upon whom the notice, if any, ought to have been served.</u>

14. We also find that the petitioner has been enjoying the MPO facilities since long.

<u>15. As such, in our considered opinion, this notice is not a proper notice and this notice should have been addressed to the petitioner whose right and the privilege is to be affected, in the event the MPO is stopped, on the basis of the allegations made in this notice dated 17.02.2010. We are of the further view, that if this kind of practices are allowed to be continued by the persons holding and exercising statutory power then it will create anarchy and indulge in arbitrariness, victimization etc. Besides, the person whose rights and interest are going to be affected has to know about the allegations brought against her.</u>

16. Therefore, in our considered opinion, a notice in which the allegations were brought against the petitioner ought to have been directly served upon or addressed to the petitioner, because it is the petitioner whose right and interest are going to be affected or curtailed on the allegations levelled against her. Besides, the inquiry or investigation held without affording the petitioner an opportunity to show cause as to why the right or the privilege enjoyed by her should not be curtailed or stopped, as the case may be, on the allegations brought against her, is clearly violative of the principle of natural justice. Moreover, we also find that the impugned order, though, called temporary, is not temporary in effect. We hold that the impugned order is arbitrary, unilatural and is contrary to the law declared in 2010 (XVIII) BLT (HCD) 303: Md. Shawkat Ali Vs. Director General & ors; 6 LG (2009) HCD 502: Md. Anwar Hossain Vs. Govt. of Bangladesh and 60 DLR 712: Emdadul Haque Vs. DG, Secondary & Higher Secondary Education.

17. In view of the above, we find merit in this rule.

<u>18. However, before parting of, we must make an observation that the authority concerned should be at liberty to initiate proceedings, if they have bonafide grounds and materials in their hands for holding an inquiry into the matter, after issuing a show cause notice asking the petitioner to explain about the allegations brought against her and then to inquire into the matter, by forming a neutral inquiry committee, as per law, if the explanation of the petitioner is not found satisfactory and then to take step according to law.</u>

<u>19. In the course of delivering the judgment, a resolution dated 12.06.2014, under signature of one Mr. Muazzam Hossain Sardar, President of the Managing Committee of Shakhipur Islamia High School, has come into our notice, in which it has been recorded that “কমিটির সদস্য জনাব এ , কে, এম আমির হোসেন প্রস্তাব রাখেন যে, হাইকোর্টের রীট আমরা বুঝি না I চূড়ান্ত ভাবে হাইকোর্টের রিটের রায় না পাওয়া পর্যন্ত রাহিমা বেগমকে বিদ্যালয় হইতে কোনরুপ বেতন ও ভাতাদি সহায়তা করা হইবে না I উহা অন্য সদস্য মেজবেউল আমিন সাহেবও সমর্থন করেন ৷ এবং রাহিমা বেগমের বেতন ভাতাদি না দেওয়ার সিদ্ধান্তে উপচ্ছিত সকলে একমত পোষণ করেন।” This clearly shows utter disrespect and reckless attitude of members of this committee to the superior court, for which they should be made answerable to answer a contempt Rule to be issued as per Article 108 of the Constitution. However, they are let off, this time, with warning and are directed to be cautions in future in performing their function having due respect to this Court.</u>

20. In view of the deliberation herein above recorded, we find merit in this rule.

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.

The impugned Memo No. ৬সি/৭৯-৭/০৬৯৩১/৭ dated 17.02.2014 is hereby declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is no legal effect. The respondents are, in consequence, directed to release the government portion of salary of the petitioner, under the MPO scheme, from the date it has been stopped, within 30(thirty) days of receiving copy of this judgment and order. No order as to cost.

End.
